Produce two consulting deliverables for NovaTrans Logistics (a plant-consolidation engagement escalated by the Board), written to `/work/output/`:

1. **Plant Consolidation Scoring Model (`.xlsx`)** with exactly 4 tabs: `Composite_Score` (rank all 19 plants, weighted model with documented rationale), `Consolidation_Scenarios` (volume redistribution for top closure candidates respecting port-access topology, with net cost impact), `Risk_Matrix` (complaint/survey cross-reference for attrition risk), `Data_Reconciliation` (verify memo claims against data; reconcile plant-code coverage across datasets).
2. **Board Decision Brief (`.docx`, max 5 pages)** with: Methodology Statement, Consolidation Recommendation (metrics + redistribution plans per candidate), Implementation Risk Assessment (grounded in specific data), and a Go/No-Go Matrix assigning each candidate exactly one of: **Close, Consolidate, or Retain-and-Monitor**. Must also address where the COO memo's priorities and the Board directive align/conflict.

Data sources: local files (COO_Engagement_Memo.docx, Customer_Satisfaction_Survey_Q4.xlsx, OrderList.csv, PlantPorts.csv) plus pinned external references in `/work/task_folder/references/` (WhCapacities.csv, WhCosts.csv, FreightRates.csv — from the Brunel University London Figshare Supply Chain Logistics Problem Dataset). No internet access.

## Instructions

- Operationalize "structurally unviable" (memo does not define it) using available data.
- Board wants 3–5 closure/consolidation candidates out of 19 plants.
- Scenario tab must respect topology: port access determines which plants can absorb volume.
- Deliverables go to `/work/output/`; helper/analysis scripts were kept in `/work/work/`.
- Todo list state: items 1–4 (data analysis, model design, Excel build) **completed**; item 5 (Word brief) — builder script written but **not yet executed**; item 6 (verify outputs) **pending**.

## Discoveries

**Data landscape:** OrderList.csv = 9,215 orders, all dated 5/26/13 (single day), 29.5M units, 183,118 weight, 46 customers; covers only **7 of 19 plants** (PLANT03, 04, 08, 09, 12, 13, 16). PLANT03 alone = 92.7% of orders / 96.9% of units. Survey (50 responses) and complaints (18) cover the same 7 plants. FreightRates (1,539 rows): only AIR/GROUND modes (no SEA), DTD/DTP only (CRF unpriceable), 9 carriers V444_0–V444_9, all lanes → PORT09, no PORT01→PORT09 lane. Order carrier `V44_3` (854 CRF orders) absent from rate card.

**Memo claim verification (reconciliation tab):** 19 plants ✓; 9,215 orders ≈ "9,000+" ✓ (with single-day caveat); late rate 2.08% (192/9,215) ✓ "≈2%" ✓; PLANT01 "1,070 units/day" & PLANT15 "11" match **stated capacity** in WhCapacities, not throughput (⚠, and neither plant has any orders); "SEA mode" ✗ not in rate card; "AIR is more expensive" ✗ **contradicted** (like-for-like PORT03→PORT09 DTD 100wt: AIR $0.31–0.71/unit vs GROUND $7.47–132.28/unit); "WhCosts has fixed+variable components" ✗ (single Cost_Per_Unit column only). Unit-scale integrity flag: 29.5M observed units vs 5,791 total stated daily capacity ≈ 5,096× (utilization % not computable; model uses relative shares).

**Composite model (weights: D1 capacity-scale 25% log-inverse, D2 handling cost 20%, D3 absorbability 20% = peer-capacity share on same port(s), D4 demand contribution 15%, D5 service 20% = 40% late + 30% severity-weighted complaints + 30% detractors, neutral 50 if no data). Tier bands: ≥65 Tier 1, 55–65 Tier 2, 45–55 watchlist, <45 retain.** Ranked scores: PLANT19 73.2, PLANT08 70.2, PLANT09 62.9, PLANT15 60.3, PLANT06 60.3 (top-5 candidates), then PLANT18 56.3, PLANT10 55.8 (watchlist), PLANT17 50.0, PLANT11 49.8, PLANT07 48.3, PLANT12 46.6, PLANT16 38.4, PLANT02 36.5, PLANT13 35.8, PLANT05 33.7, PLANT01 32.6, PLANT14 31.5, PLANT04 19.1, PLANT03 15.7.

PLANT19: 0 orders → deltas $0. PLANT08: 102 orders/277,008 units/5 customers → Δwh **+$4,281**, Δfreight $0 (same port), late orders 18→~1. PLANT09: 12 orders/223,830 units/2 customers → Δwh **+$16,394**, Δfreight $0. PLANT15 (unique PORT08) & PLANT06 (shares PORT06 with PLANT05): 0 volume, administrative consolidation. Totals: variable cost +$20,675/period, $875k one-off — business case rests on service recovery + unquantifiable fixed-cost release (R-08). **PLANT16 sensitivity S-1:** migrating unique-port PORT09 role to PORT04 saves **$338,653 wh + $2,484 freight = $341,137/period** (all 173 orders re-priced), but TPT rises (currently 0–1 days; PORT04 lanes 0–5) → retained Phase 1, lead Phase-2 candidate.

**Risk matrix:** PLANT08 HIGH (top customer V555555555_14 = 77/102 orders = 75.5%; 18 late/17.65%; complaints C-002 open 22d, C-006 open, C-008 High; detractors CUST-026/011/007/027; sat 3.12). PLANT09 HIGH (V55555555_7 = 11/12 = 91.7%; worst sat 2.50; complaints C-009 open 22d, C-014 High open; detractors CUST-030/034/025/021). PLANT19/15/06 LOW (no customers). 6/18 complaints (33%) on candidates incl. both High-severity cases; absorbers PLANT12/PLANT13 carry open escalations C-016/C-017. Contagion: 16/46 order-book customers and 12 survey respondents span multiple plants.

**Go/No-Go:** PLANT19 CLOSE; PLANT08 CONSOLIDATE; PLANT09 CONSOLIDATE; PLANT15 CONSOLIDATE (administrative); PLANT06 CONSOLIDATE; watchlist PLANT18/PLANT10/PLANT16 RETAIN-AND-MONITOR.

**Environment:** Python 3.12, pandas 2.3.3, openpyxl 3.1.5, python-docx available. **No LibreOffice** (formulas can't be server-recalculated; composite formulas hand-verified: e.g., PLANT19 = .25×100+.2×16.1+.2×99.7+.15×100+.2×50 = 73.2 ✓).

[{"content": "## Goal

Produce two consulting deliverables for NovaTrans Logistics (a plant-consolidation engagement escalated by the Board), written to `/work/output/`:

1. **Plant Consolidation Scoring Model (`.xlsx`)** with exactly 4 tabs: `Composite_Score` (rank all 19 plants, weighted model with documented rationale), `Consolidation_Scenarios` (volume redistribution for top closure candidates respecting port-access topology, with net cost impact), `Risk_Matrix` (complaint/survey cross-reference for attrition risk), `Data_Reconciliation` (verify memo claims against data; reconcile plant-code coverage across datasets).
2. **Board Decision Brief (`.docx`, max 5 pages)** with: Methodology Statement, Consolidation Recommendation (metrics + redistribution plans per candidate), Implementation Risk Assessment (grounded in specific data), and a Go/No-Go Matrix assigning each candidate exactly one of: **Close, Consolidate, or Retain-and-Monitor**. Must also address where the COO memo's priorities and the Board directive align/conflict.

Data sources: local files (COO_Engagement_Memo.docx, Customer_Satisfaction_Survey_Q4.xlsx, OrderList.csv, PlantPorts.csv) plus pinned external references in `/work/task_folder/references/` (WhCapacities.csv, WhCosts.csv, FreightRates.csv — from the Brunel University London Figshare Supply Chain Logistics Problem Dataset). No internet access.

## Instructions

- Operationalize "structurally unviable" (memo does not define it) using available data.
- Board wants 3–5 closure/consolidation candidates out of 19 plants.
- Scenario tab must respect topology: port access determines which plants can absorb volume.
- Deliverables go to `/work/output/`; helper/analysis scripts were kept in `/work/work/`.
- Todo list state: items 1–4 (data analysis, model design, Excel build) **completed**; item 5 (Word brief) — builder script written but **not yet executed**; item 6 (verify outputs) **pending**.

## Discoveries

**Data landscape:** OrderList.csv = 9,215 orders, all dated 5/26/13 (single day), 29.5M units, 183,118 weight, 46 customers; covers only **7 of 19 plants** (PLANT03, 04, 08, 09, 12, 13, 16). PLANT03 alone = 92.7% of orders / 96.9% of units. Survey (50 responses) and complaints (18) cover the same 7 plants. FreightRates (1,539 rows): only AIR/GROUND modes (no SEA), DTD/DTP only (CRF unpriceable), 9 carriers V444_0–V444_9, all lanes → PORT09, no PORT01→PORT09 lane. Order carrier `V44_3` (854 CRF orders) absent from rate card.

**Memo claim verification (reconciliation tab):** 19 plants ✓; 9,215 orders ≈ "9,000+" ✓ (with single-day caveat); late rate 2.08% (192/9,215) ✓ "≈2%" ✓; PLANT01 "1,070 units/day" & PLANT15 "11" match **stated capacity** in WhCapacities, not throughput (⚠, and neither plant has any orders); "SEA mode" ✗ not in rate card; "AIR is more expensive" ✗ **contradicted** (like-for-like PORT03→PORT09 DTD 100wt: AIR $0.31–0.71/unit vs GROUND $7.47–132.28/unit); "WhCosts has fixed+variable components" ✗ (single Cost_Per_Unit column only). Unit-scale integrity flag: 29.5M observed units vs 5,791 total stated daily capacity ≈ 5,096× (utilization % not computable; model uses relative shares).

Produce two consulting deliverables for NovaTrans Logistics (a plant-consolidation engagement escalated by the Board), written to `/work/output/`:

1. **Plant Consolidation Scoring Model (`.xlsx`)** with exactly 4 tabs: `Composite_Score` (rank all 19 plants, weighted model with documented rationale), `Consolidation_Scenarios` (volume redistribution for top closure candidates respecting port-access topology, with net cost impact), `Risk_Matrix` (complaint/survey cross-reference for attrition risk), `Data_Reconciliation` (verify memo claims against data; reconcile plant-code coverage across datasets).
2. **Board Decision Brief (`.docx`, max 5 pages)** with: Methodology Statement, Consolidation Recommendation (metrics + redistribution plans per candidate), Implementation Risk Assessment (grounded in specific data), and a Go/No-Go Matrix assigning each candidate exactly one of: **Close, Consolidate, or Retain-and-Monitor**. Must also address where the COO memo's priorities and the Board directive align/conflict.

Data sources: local files (COO_Engagement_Memo.docx, Customer_Satisfaction_Survey_Q4.xlsx, OrderList.csv, PlantPorts.csv) plus pinned external references in `/work/task_folder/references/` (WhCapacities.csv, WhCosts.csv, FreightRates.csv — from the Brunel University London Figshare Supply Chain Logistics Problem Dataset). No internet access.

## Instructions

- Operationalize "structurally unviable" (memo does not define it) using available data.
- Board wants 3–5 closure/consolidation candidates out of 19 plants.
- Scenario tab must respect topology: port access determines which plants can absorb volume.
- Deliverables go to `/work/output/`; helper/analysis scripts were kept in `/work/work/`.
- Todo list state: items 1–4 (data analysis, model design, Excel build) **completed**; item 5 (Word brief) — builder script written but **not yet executed**; item 6 (verify outputs) **pending**.

## Discoveries

**Data landscape:** OrderList.csv = 9,215 orders, all dated 5/26/13 (single day), 29.5M units, 183,118 weight, 46 customers; covers only **7 of 19 plants** (PLANT03, 04, 08, 09, 12, 13, 16). PLANT03 alone = 92.7% of orders / 96.9% of units. Survey (50 responses) and complaints (18) cover the same 7 plants. FreightRates (1,539 rows): only AIR/GROUND modes (no SEA), DTD/DTP only (CRF unpriceable), 9 carriers V444_0–V444_9, all lanes → PORT09, no PORT01→PORT09 lane. Order carrier `V44_3` (854 CRF orders) absent from rate card.

**Memo claim verification (reconciliation tab):** 19 plants ✓; 9,215 orders ≈ "9,000+" ✓ (with single-day caveat); late rate 2.08% (192/9,215) ✓ "≈2%" ✓; PLANT01 "1,070 units/day" & PLANT15 "11" match **stated capacity** in WhCapacities, not throughput (⚠, and neither plant has any orders); "SEA mode" ✗ not in rate card; "AIR is more expensive" ✗ **contradicted** (like-for-like PORT03→PORT09 DTD 100wt: AIR $0.31–0.71/unit vs GROUND $7.47–132.28/unit); "WhCosts has fixed+variable components" ✗ (single Cost_Per_Unit column only). Unit-scale integrity flag: 29.5M observed units vs 5,791 total stated daily capacity ≈ 5,096× (utilization % not computable; model uses relative shares).

**Composite model (weights: D1 capacity-scale 25% log-inverse, D2 handling cost 20%, D3 absorbability 20% = peer-capacity share on same port(s), D4 demand contribution 15%, D5 service 20% = 40% late + 30% severity-weighted complaints + 30% detractors, neutral 50 if no data). Tier bands: ≥65 Tier 1, 55–65 Tier 2, 45–55 watchlist, <45 retain.** Ranked scores: PLANT19 73.2, PLANT08 70.2, PLANT09 62.9, PLANT15 60.3, PLANT06 60.3 (top-5 candidates), then PLANT18 56.3, PLANT10 55.8 (watchlist), PLANT17 50.0, PLANT11 49.8, PLANT07 48.3, PLANT12 46.6, PLANT16 38.4, PLANT02 36.5, PLANT13 35.8, PLANT05 33.7, PLANT01 32.6, PLANT14 31.5, PLANT04 19.1, PLANT03 15.7.

**Scenario economics (per order-book period; $175k one-off transition per plant as documented assumption):** PORT04 absorber allocation (capacity-weighted, excluding closing plants): PLANT03 49.6%, PLANT13 24.0%, PLANT11 16.2%, PLANT12 10.2%. PLANT19: 0 orders → deltas $0. PLANT08: 102 orders/277,008 units/5 customers → Δwh **+$4,281**, Δfreight $0 (same port), late orders 18→~1. PLANT09: 12 orders/223,830 units/2 customers → Δwh **+$16,394**, Δfreight $0. PLANT15 (unique PORT08) & PLANT06 (shares PORT06 with PLANT05): 0 volume, administrative consolidation. Totals: variable cost +$20,675/period, $875k one-off — business case rests on service recovery + unquantifiable fixed-cost release (R-08). **PLANT16 sensitivity S-1:** migrating unique-port PORT09 role to PORT04 saves **$338,653 wh + $2,484 freight = $341,137/period** (all 173 orders re-priced), but TPT rises (currently 0–1 days; PORT04 lanes 0–5) → retained Phase 1, lead Phase-2 candidate.

**Risk matrix:** PLANT08 HIGH (top customer V555555555_14 = 77/102 orders = 75.5%; 18 late/17.65%; complaints C-002 open 22d, C-006 open, C-008 High; detractors CUST-026/011/007/027; sat 3.12). PLANT09 HIGH (V55555555_7 = 11/12 = 91.7%; worst sat 2.50; complaints C-009 open 22d, C-014 High open; detractors CUST-030/034/025/021). PLANT19/15/06 LOW (no customers). 6/18 complaints (33%) on candidates incl. both High-severity cases; absorbers PLANT12/PLANT13 carry open escalations C-016/C-017. Contagion: 16/46 order-book customers and 12 survey respondents span multiple plants.

**Go/No-Go:** PLANT19 CLOSE; PLANT08 CONSOLIDATE; PLANT09 CONSOLIDATE; PLANT15 CONSOLIDATE (administrative); PLANT06 CONSOLIDATE; watchlist PLANT18/PLANT10/PLANT16 RETAIN-AND-MONITOR.

**Environment:** Python 3.12, pandas 2.3.3, openpyxl 3.1.5, python-docx available. **No LibreOffice** (formulas can't be server-recalculated; composite formulas hand-verified: e.g., PLANT19 = .25×100+.2×16.1+.2×99.7+.15×100+.2×50 = 73.2 ✓).

[{"content": "[0] NOVATRANS LOGISTICS
[1] Delivering Excellence Across Every Mile
[3] INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
[5] DATE:  January 15, 2024
[6] TO:  Operations Consulting Team
[7] FROM:  David Chen, Chief Operating Officer, NovaTrans Logistics
[8] SUBJECT:  Engagement Brief: Distribution Network Efficiency Review
[10] 1. Background & Context
[11] NovaTrans Logistics is a mid-sized, port-based logistics company specializing in freight distribution and supply chain fulfillment. We currently operate 19 distribution plants strategically positioned across our network, handling the movement of goods between manufacturing origins, inland warehouses, and port terminals.
[12] On an annual basis, our network processes roughly 9,000+ individual shipments spanning multiple transportation modes, including SEA, AIR, and ROAD. We serve a diverse portfolio of customers under three distinct service levels:
[13] CRF (Cross-dock Freight) -- Goods are consolidated at a cross-dock facility and forwarded without long-term storage, optimizing transit speed.
[14] DTD (Door-to-Door) -- Full end-to-end delivery from origin to the customer's designated receiving location.
[15] DTP (Door-to-Port) -- Delivery from the origin point to the designated port terminal, where the customer or a third-party forwarder assumes custody.
[16] Our ERP system captures detailed transactional data for every order, including origin/destination plant codes, shipment dates, carrier assignments, freight costs, and warehouse throughput metrics. This data forms the foundation for the analysis we are requesting.
[17] 2. Problem Statement
[18] Despite steady revenue growth over the past three fiscal years, our operating margins have come under increasing pressure. Preliminary internal reviews point to several areas of concern that require rigorous, data-driven investigation:
[19] Rising Freight Costs. Overall freight expenditure has increased disproportionately relative to shipment volume. The AIR transportation mode, in particular, exhibits significantly higher per-unit costs compared to SEA and ROAD, yet continues to be utilized for shipments where alternative modes may be viable. We need a clear understanding of cost drivers across carriers and routes.
[20] Late Shipments & Customer Dissatisfaction. Approximately 2% of all orders ship late relative to their scheduled ship date. While this figure may appear modest, it translates to a meaningful number of affected customers each quarter, eroding satisfaction and jeopardizing key accounts. Our Q4 2023 customer satisfaction survey data reinforces this concern.
[21] Uneven Warehouse Utilization. Warehouse throughput varies dramatically across our plant network. For example, PLANT01 handles approximately 1,070 units per day, making it one of our highest-volume facilities, while PLANT15 processes only around 11 units per day. This imbalance raises questions about capacity allocation, fixed cost absorption, and whether certain low-volume plants should be consolidated or repurposed.
[22] Carrier & Route Cost Variability. We suspect that significant cost-efficiency differences exist between carrier-route combinations. Some carriers may deliver comparable service levels at materially lower rates on specific lanes, but we lack a consolidated view to validate this hypothesis and act on it.
[23] 3. Scope of Engagement
[24] We are engaging your team to conduct a comprehensive review of our distribution network operations. Specifically, we request that you:
[25] Analyze the order and shipment data to identify operational bottlenecks, including transit-time outliers, mode-selection inefficiencies, and demand concentration patterns.
[26] Evaluate freight cost efficiency across carriers, transportation modes, and specific origin-destination routes. Identify lanes where cost savings are achievable without degrading service quality.
[27] Assess warehouse capacity utilization across all 19 plants. Determine which facilities are over- or under-utilized relative to their stated capacity and recommend rebalancing strategies.
[28] Identify root causes of late shipments. Correlate late-shipment data with plant origin, carrier assignment, service level, and transportation mode to isolate the primary drivers of delays.
[29] Provide actionable recommendations supported by data. Each recommendation should include an estimated impact (cost savings, service improvement, or capacity optimization) and an implementation priority ranking.
[30] 4. Available Data
[31] The following data exports and reference materials are provided for your analysis. Source files may reflect different operating periods unless otherwise noted:
[33] 5. Expected Deliverables
[34] Upon completion of the engagement, we expect the following deliverables:
[35] Excel-Based Analysis Workbook. A comprehensive workbook containing separate tabs for each analytical dimension (freight cost analysis, warehouse utilization, late shipment analysis, carrier/route comparison, etc.). Each tab should include source data summaries, pivot analyses, charts where appropriate, and key findings highlighted in a consistent format.
[36] Executive Summary Report (Word Document). A standalone Word document (maximum 10 pages) summarizing the engagement findings, key insights, and prioritized recommendations. This document will be circulated to the executive leadership team and should be written at a level appropriate for a C-suite audience. Include an executive summary on the first page, followed by detailed sections for each analytical area, and conclude with a prioritized action plan.
[37] 6. Timeline & Presentation
[38] The deadline for submission of all deliverables is two (2) weeks from the date of this memorandum. Upon submission, the consulting team will be invited to present findings and recommendations to the NovaTrans executive leadership team, including the CEO, CFO, VP of Operations, and VP of Supply Chain.
[39] Please allocate approximately 45 minutes for the presentation, followed by a 15-minute Q&A session. Presentation materials may be prepared in addition to the deliverables listed above, at your discretion.
[40] 7. Points of Contact
[41] For any questions regarding data interpretation, system access, or scope clarifications, please direct inquiries to:
[42] Primary: David Chen, COO -- david.chen@novatrans-logistics.com
[43] Secondary: Maria Santos, Director of Operations -- maria.santos@novatrans-logistics.com
[44] Data/IT: James Park, Senior Data Analyst -- james.park@novatrans-logistics.com
[47] We look forward to a productive engagement and anticipate that your analysis will provide the data-driven foundation needed to optimize our distribution network and strengthen our competitive position.
[49] Regards,

[14] DTD (Door-to-Door) -- Full end-to-end delivery from origin to the customer's designated receiving location.
[15] DTP (Door-to-Port) -- Delivery from the origin point to the designated port terminal, where the customer or a third-party forwarder assumes custody.

bullet('Customer concentration. PLANT08\'s top customer V555555555_14 holds 77 of 102 orders (75.5%) and ships via two plants; PLANT09\'s V55555555_7 holds 11 of 12 orders (91.7%). Migrations for these accounts need white-glove sequencing, not big-bang cutovers.')

bullet('Open complaints on candidate plants. 6 of 18 Q4 complaints (33%) sit on candidates, including the only two High-severity cases (C-008 PLANT08, C-014 PLANT09) and two 22-day-old open cases (C-002, C-009). bullet('Network concentration. PLANT03 already carries 92.7% of orders and 96.9% of units. The capacity-share allocation caps PLANT03 at 49.6% of redistributed volume; the Board should treat any further PLANT03 dependence as a standing risk metric.')

bullet('Data risks. [1] Delivering Excellence Across Every Mile

[5] DATE:  January 15, 2024
[6] TO:  Operations Consulting Team
[7] FROM:  David Chen, Chief Operating Officer, NovaTrans Logistics
[8] SUBJECT:  Engagement Brief: Distribution Network Efficiency Review
[10] 1. Background & Context
[11] NovaTrans Logistics is a mid-sized, port-based logistics company specializing in freight distribution and supply chain fulfillment. We currently operate 19 distribution plants strategically positioned across our network, handling the movement of goods between manufacturing origins, inland warehouses, and port terminals.
[12] On an annual basis, our network processes roughly 9,000+ individual shipments spanning multiple transportation modes, including SEA, AIR, and ROAD. We serve a diverse portfolio of customers under three distinct service levels:
[13] CRF (Cross-dock Freight) -- Goods are consolidated at a cross-dock facility and forwarded without long-term storage, optimizing transit speed.
[14] DTD (Door-to-Door) -- Full end-to-end delivery from origin to the customer's designated receiving location.
[15] DTP (Door-to-Port) -- Delivery from the origin point to the designated port terminal, where the customer or a third-party forwarder assumes custody.
[16] Our ERP system captures detailed transactional data for every order, including origin/destination plant codes, shipment dates, carrier assignments, freight costs, and warehouse throughput metrics. This data forms the foundation for the analysis we are requesting.
[17] 2. Problem Statement
[18] Despite steady revenue growth over the past three fiscal years, our operating margins have come under increasing pressure. Preliminary internal reviews point to several areas of concern that require rigorous, data-driven investigation:
[19] Rising Freight Costs. Overall freight expenditure has increased disproportionately relative to shipment volume. The AIR transportation mode, in particular, exhibits significantly higher per-unit costs compared to SEA and ROAD, yet continues to be utilized for shipments where alternative modes may be viable. We need a clear understanding of cost drivers across carriers and routes.
[20] Late Shipments & Customer Dissatisfaction. Approximately 2% of all orders ship late relative to their scheduled ship date. While this figure may appear modest, it translates to a meaningful number of affected customers each quarter, eroding satisfaction and jeopardizing key accounts. Our Q4 2023 customer satisfaction survey data reinforces this concern.
[21] Uneven Warehouse Utilization. Warehouse throughput varies dramatically across our plant network. For example, PLANT01 handles approximately 1,070 units per day, making it one of our highest-volume facilities, while PLANT15 processes only around 11 units per day. This imbalance raises questions about capacity allocation, fixed cost absorption, and whether certain low-volume plants should be consolidated or repurposed.
[22] Carrier & Route Cost Variability. We suspect that significant cost-efficiency differences exist between carrier-route combinations. Some carriers may deliver comparable service levels at materially lower rates on specific lanes, but we lack a consolidated view to validate this hypothesis and act on it.
[23] 3. Scope of Engagement
[24] We are engaging your team to conduct a comprehensive review of our distribution network operations. Specifically, we request that you:
[25] Analyze the order and shipment data to identify operational bottlenecks, including transit-time outliers, mode-selection inefficiencies, and demand concentration patterns.
[26] Evaluate freight cost efficiency across carriers, transportation modes, and specific origin-destination routes. Identify lanes where cost savings are achievable without degrading service quality.
[27] Assess warehouse capacity utilization across all 19 plants. Determine which facilities are over- or under-utilized relative to their stated capacity and recommend rebalancing strategies.
[28] Identify root causes of late shipments. Correlate late-shipment data with plant origin, carrier assignment, service level, and transportation mode to isolate the primary drivers of delays.
[29] Provide actionable recommendations supported by data. Each recommendation should include an estimated impact (cost savings, service improvement, or capacity optimization) and an implementation priority ranking.

[3] INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
[5] DATE:  January 15, 2024
[6] TO:  Operations Consulting Team
[7] FROM:  David Chen, Chief Operating Officer, NovaTrans Logistics
[8] SUBJECT:  Engagement Brief: Distribution Network Efficiency Review
[10] 1. Background & Context
[11] NovaTrans Logistics is a mid-sized, port-based logistics company specializing in freight distribution and supply chain fulfillment. We currently operate 19 distribution plants strategically positioned across our network, handling the movement of goods between manufacturing origins, inland warehouses, and port terminals.
[12] On an annual basis, our network processes roughly 9,000+ individual shipments spanning multiple transportation modes, including SEA, AIR, and ROAD. We serve a diverse portfolio of customers under three distinct service levels:
[13] CRF (Cross-dock Freight) -- Goods are consolidated at a cross-dock facility and forwarded without long-term storage, optimizing transit speed.
[14] DTD (Door-to-Door) -- Full end-to-end delivery from origin to the customer's designated receiving location.
[15] DTP (Door-to-Port) -- Delivery from the origin point to the designated port terminal, where the customer or a third-party forwarder assumes custody.
[16] Our ERP system captures detailed transactional data for every order, including origin/destination plant codes, shipment dates, carrier assignments, freight costs, and warehouse throughput metrics. This data forms the foundation for the analysis we are requesting.
[17] 2. Problem Statement
[18] Despite steady revenue growth over the past three fiscal years, our operating margins have come under increasing pressure. Preliminary internal reviews point to several areas of concern that require rigorous, data-driven investigation:
[19] Rising Freight Costs. Overall freight expenditure has increased disproportionately relative to shipment volume. The AIR transportation mode, in particular, exhibits significantly higher per-unit costs compared to SEA and ROAD, yet continues to be utilized for shipments where alternative modes may be viable. We need a clear understanding of cost drivers across carriers and routes.
[20] Late Shipments & Customer Dissatisfaction. Approximately 2% of all orders ship late relative to their scheduled ship date. While this figure may appear modest, it translates to a meaningful number of affected customers each quarter, eroding satisfaction and jeopardizing key accounts. Our Q4 2023 customer satisfaction survey data reinforces this concern.
[21] Uneven Warehouse Utilization. Warehouse throughput varies dramatically across our plant network. For example, PLANT01 handles approximately 1,070 units per day, making it one of our highest-volume facilities, while PLANT15 processes only around 11 units per day. This imbalance raises questions about capacity allocation, fixed cost absorption, and whether certain low-volume plants should be consolidated or repurposed.
[22] Carrier & Route Cost Variability. We suspect that significant cost-efficiency differences exist between carrier-route combinations. Some carriers may deliver comparable service levels at materially lower rates on specific lanes, but we lack a consolidated view to validate this hypothesis and act on it.
[23] 3. Scope of Engagement
[24] We are engaging your team to conduct a comprehensive review of our distribution network operations. Specifically, we request that you:
[25] Analyze the order and shipment data to identify operational bottlenecks, including transit-time outliers, mode-selection inefficiencies, and demand concentration patterns.
[26] Evaluate freight cost efficiency across carriers, transportation modes, and specific origin-destination routes. Identify lanes where cost savings are achievable without degrading service quality.
[27] Assess warehouse capacity utilization across all 19 plants. Determine which facilities are over- or under-utilized relative to their stated capacity and recommend rebalancing strategies.
[28] Identify root causes of late shipments. Correlate late-shipment data with plant origin, carrier assignment, service level, and transportation mode to isolate the primary drivers of delays.
[29] Provide actionable recommendations supported by data. Each recommendation should include an estimated impact (cost savings, service improvement, or capacity optimization) and an implementation priority ranking.
[30] 4. Available Data
[31] The following data exports and reference materials are provided for your analysis. Source files may reflect different operating periods unless otherwise noted:
[33] 5. Expected Deliverables
[34] Upon completion of the engagement, we expect the following deliverables:
[35] Excel-Based Analysis Workbook. A comprehensive workbook containing separate tabs for each analytical dimension (freight cost analysis, warehouse utilization, late shipment analysis, carrier/route comparison, etc.). Each tab should include source data summaries, pivot analyses, charts where appropriate, and key findings highlighted in a consistent format.
[36] Executive Summary Report (Word Document). A standalone Word document (maximum 10 pages) summarizing the engagement findings, key insights, and prioritized recommendations. This document will be circulated to the executive leadership team and should be written at a level appropriate for a C-suite audience. Include an executive summary on the first page, followed by detailed sections for each analytical area, and conclude with a prioritized action plan.
[37] 6. Timeline & Presentation
[38] The deadline for submission of all deliverables is two (2) weeks from the date of this memorandum. Upon submission, the consulting team will be invited to present findings and recommendations to the NovaTrans executive leadership team, including the CEO, CFO, VP of Operations, and VP of Supply Chain.
[39] Please allocate approximately 45 minutes for the presentation, followed by a 15-minute Q&A session. Presentation materials may be prepared in addition to the deliverables listed above, at your discretion.
[40] 7. Points of Contact
[41] For any questions regarding data interpretation, system access, or scope clarifications, please direct inquiries to:
[42] Primary: David Chen, COO -- david.chen@novatrans-logistics.com
[43] Secondary: Maria Santos, Director of Operations -- maria.santos@novatrans-logistics.com

[{"content": "[0] NOVATRANS LOGISTICS
[1] Delivering Excellence Across Every Mile
[3] INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
[5] DATE:  January 15, 2024
[6] TO:  Operations Consulting Team
[7] FROM:  David Chen, Chief Operating Officer, NovaTrans Logistics
[8] SUBJECT:  Engagement Brief: Distribution Network Efficiency Review
[10] 1. Background & Context
[11] NovaTrans Logistics is a mid-sized, port-based logistics company specializing in freight distribution and supply chain fulfillment. We currently operate 19 distribution plants strategically positioned across our network, handling the movement of goods between manufacturing origins, inland warehouses, and port terminals.
[12] On an annual basis, our network processes roughly 9,000+ individual shipments spanning multiple transportation modes, including SEA, AIR, and ROAD. We serve a diverse portfolio of customers under three distinct service levels:
[13] CRF (Cross-dock Freight) -- Goods are consolidated at a cross-dock facility and forwarded without long-term storage, optimizing transit speed.
[14] DTD (Door-to-Door) -- Full end-to-end delivery from origin to the customer's designated receiving location.
[15] DTP (Door-to-Port) -- Delivery from the origin point to the designated port terminal, where the customer or a third-party forwarder assumes custody.
[16] Our ERP system captures detailed transactional data for every order, including origin/destination plant codes, shipment dates, carrier assignments, freight costs, and warehouse throughput metrics. This data forms the foundation for the analysis we are requesting.
[17] 2. Problem Statement
[18] Despite steady revenue growth over the past three fiscal years, our operating margins have come under increasing pressure. Preliminary internal reviews point to several areas of concern that require rigorous, data-driven investigation:
[19] Rising Freight Costs. Overall freight expenditure has increased disproportionately relative to shipment volume. The AIR transportation mode, in particular, exhibits significantly higher per-unit costs compared to SEA and ROAD, yet continues to be utilized for shipments where alternative modes may be viable. We need a clear understanding of cost drivers across carriers and routes.
[20] Late Shipments & Customer Dissatisfaction. Approximately 2% of all orders ship late relative to their scheduled ship date. While this figure may appear modest, it translates to a meaningful number of affected customers each quarter, eroding satisfaction and jeopardizing key accounts. Our Q4 2023 customer satisfaction survey data reinforces this concern.
[21] Uneven Warehouse Utilization. Warehouse throughput varies dramatically across our plant network. For example, PLANT01 handles approximately 1,070 units per day, making it one of our highest-volume facilities, while PLANT15 processes only around 11 units per day. This imbalance raises questions about capacity allocation, fixed cost absorption, and whether certain low-volume plants should be consolidated or repurposed.
[22] Carrier & Route Cost Variability. We suspect that significant cost-efficiency differences exist between carrier-route combinations. Some carriers may deliver comparable service levels at materially lower rates on specific lanes, but we lack a consolidated view to validate this hypothesis and act on it.
[23] 3. Scope of Engagement
[24] We are engaging your team to conduct a comprehensive review of our distribution network operations. Specifically, we request that you:
[25] Analyze the order and shipment data to identify operational bottlenecks, including transit-time outliers, mode-selection inefficiencies, and demand concentration patterns.
[26] Evaluate freight cost efficiency across carriers, transportation modes, and specific origin-destination routes. Identify lanes where cost savings are achievable without degrading service quality.
[27] Assess warehouse capacity utilization across all 19 plants. Determine which facilities are over- or under-utilized relative to their stated capacity and recommend rebalancing strategies.
[28] Identify root causes of late shipments. Correlate late-shipment data with plant origin, carrier assignment, service level, and transportation mode to isolate the primary drivers of delays.
[29] Provide actionable recommendations supported by data. Each recommendation should include an estimated impact (cost savings, service improvement, or capacity optimization) and an implementation priority ranking.
[30] 4. Available Data
[31] The following data exports and reference materials are provided for your analysis. Source files may reflect different operating periods unless otherwise noted:
[33] 5. Expected Deliverables
[34] Upon completion of the engagement, we expect the following deliverables:
[35] Excel-Based Analysis Workbook. A comprehensive workbook containing separate tabs for each analytical dimension (freight cost analysis, warehouse utilization, late shipment analysis, carrier/route comparison, etc.). Each tab should include source data summaries, pivot analyses, charts where appropriate, and key findings highlighted in a consistent format.
[36] Executive Summary Report (Word Document). A standalone Word document (maximum 10 pages) summarizing the engagement findings, key insights, and prioritized recommendations. This document will be circulated to the executive leadership team and should be written at a level appropriate for a C-suite audience. Include an executive summary on the first page, followed by detailed sections for each analytical area, and conclude with a prioritized action plan.
[37] 6. Timeline & Presentation
[38] The deadline for submission of all deliverables is two (2) weeks from the date of this memorandum. Upon submission, the consulting team will be invited to present findings and recommendations to the NovaTrans executive leadership team, including the CEO, CFO, VP of Operations, and VP of Supply Chain.
[39] Please allocate approximately 45 minutes for the presentation, followed by a 15-minute Q&A session. Presentation materials may be prepared in addition to the deliverables listed above, at your discretion.
[40] 7. Points of Contact
[41] For any questions regarding data interpretation, system access, or scope clarifications, please direct inquiries to:
[42] Primary: David Chen, COO -- david.chen@novatrans-logistics.com
[43] Secondary: Maria Santos, Director of Operations -- maria.santos@novatrans-logistics.com
[44] Data/IT: James Park, Senior Data Analyst -- james.park@novatrans-logistics.com
[47] We look forward to a productive engagement and anticipate that your analysis will provide the data-driven foundation needed to optimize our distribution network and strengthen our competitive position.
[49] Regards,
[51] David Chen
[52] Chief Operating Officer
[53] NovaTrans Logistics

PLANT15 processes only around 11 units per day" → These figures exactly match WhCapacities "Daily_Capacity" (1070 and 11), NOT throughput from OrderList. So the memo conflates stated daily capacity with actual throughput. That's a reconciliation finding: the memo describes capacity figures as "throughput," but the data shows these are stated capacities. Also PLANT01 and PLANT15 have NO orders in OrderList at all.
- "19 distribution plants" → WhCapacities has 19 plants ✓, but OrderList only covers 7. PlantPorts covers all 19. Survey/Complaint data covers PLANT03, 04, 08, 09, 12, 13, 16 (same 7 as OrderList).

Plant coverage reconciliation:
- WhCapacities: 19 plants
- WhCosts: 19 plants
- PlantPorts: 19 plants
- OrderList: 7 plants (PLANT03, 04, 08, 09, 12, 13, 16)
- Survey: PLANT03, 04, 08, 09, 12, 13, 16
- Complaints: PLANT03, 04, 08, 09, 12, 13, 16 (let me verify: C-001 PLANT03, C-002 PLANT08, C-003 PLANT03, C-004 PLANT09, C-005 PLANT03, C-006 PLANT08, C-007 PLANT16, C-008 PLANT08, C-009 PLANT09, C-010 PLANT12, C-011 PLANT03, C-012 PLANT03, C-013 PLANT16, C-014 PLANT09, C-015 PLANT04, C-016 PLANT12, C-017 PLANT13, C-018 PLANT13) → plants {03, 04, 08, 09, 12, 13, 16} = same 7.

This is a big deal for the analysis: we can only compute volume-based metrics for 7 plants. For the other 12, we have capacity, cost, and port data but no observed shipments.

Network topology (PlantPorts):

So plants sharing a port can absorb each other's volume (per the task: "port access determines which plants can absorb volume from others").

Capacity (daily):

Now the composite scoring model. Dimensions to operationalize "structurally unviable":

1. **Scale / volume dependence** (throughput observed or capacity): plants with tiny capacity can't absorb fixed costs. But we need to be careful: capacity is "stated daily capacity". Observed volume from OrderList for 7 plants.

2. **Warehouse cost per unit** (WhCosts): high unit cost = uncompetitive.

3. **Utilization** (observed daily throughput vs capacity). For the 7 plants with order data, compute observed units/day. The dataset is one day (5/26/13), so units on that day = daily throughput. E.g., PLANT03: 28.6M units in one day?? vs capacity 1013/day → 28,000x over capacity. That's odd. Unit_Quant total is 29.5M units in one day. This is the classic Brunel dataset quirk (units are in grams? "Unit quantities" of product... [10] 1. Background & Context
[11] NovaTrans Logistics is a mid-sized, port-based logistics company specializing in freight distribution and supply chain fulfillment. We currently operate 19 distribution plants strategically positioned across our network, handling the movement of goods between manufacturing origins, inland warehouses, and port terminals.
[12] On an annual basis, our network processes roughly 9,000+ individual shipments spanning multiple transportation modes, including SEA, AIR, and ROAD. We serve a diverse portfolio of customers under three distinct service levels:
[13] CRF (Cross-dock Freight) -- Goods are consolidated at a cross-dock facility and forwarded without long-term storage, optimizing transit speed.
[14] DTD (Door-to-Door) -- Full end-to-end delivery from origin to the customer's designated receiving location.
[15] DTP (Door-to-Port) -- Delivery from the origin point to the designated port terminal, where the customer or a third-party forwarder assumes custody.
[16] Our ERP system captures detailed transactional data for every order, including origin/destination plant codes, shipment dates, carrier assignments, freight costs, and warehouse throughput metrics. This data forms the foundation for the analysis we are requesting.
[17] 2. Problem Statement
[18] Despite steady revenue growth over the past three fiscal years, our operating margins have come under increasing pressure. Preliminary internal reviews point to several areas of concern that require rigorous, data-driven investigation:
[19] Rising Freight Costs. Overall freight expenditure has increased disproportionately relative to shipment volume. The AIR transportation mode, in particular, exhibits significantly higher per-unit costs compared to SEA and ROAD, yet continues to be utilized for shipments where alternative modes may be viable. We need a clear understanding of cost drivers across carriers and routes.
[20] Late Shipments & Customer Dissatisfaction. Approximately 2% of all orders ship late relative to their scheduled ship date. While this figure may appear modest, it translates to a meaningful number of affected customers each quarter, eroding satisfaction and jeopardizing key accounts. Our Q4 2023 customer satisfaction survey data reinforces this concern.
[21] Uneven Warehouse Utilization. Warehouse throughput varies dramatically across our plant network. For example, PLANT01 handles approximately 1,070 units per day, making it one of our highest-volume facilities, while PLANT15 processes only around 11 units per day. This imbalance raises questions about capacity allocation, fixed cost absorption, and whether certain low-volume plants should be consolidated or repurposed.
[22] Carrier & Route Cost Variability. We suspect that significant cost-efficiency differences exist between carrier-route combinations. Some carriers may deliver comparable service levels at materially lower rates on specific lanes, but we lack a consolidated view to validate this hypothesis and act on it.
[23] 3. Scope of Engagement
[24] We are engaging your team to conduct a comprehensive review of our distribution network operations. Specifically, we request that you:
[25] Analyze the order and shipment data to identify operational bottlenecks, including transit-time outliers, mode-selection inefficiencies, and demand concentration patterns.
[26] Evaluate freight cost efficiency across carriers, transportation modes, and specific origin-destination routes. Identify lanes where cost savings are achievable without degrading service quality.
[27] Assess warehouse capacity utilization across all 19 plants. Determine which facilities are over- or under-utilized relative to their stated capacity and recommend rebalancing strategies.
[28] Identify root causes of late shipments. Correlate late-shipment data with plant origin, carrier assignment, service level, and transportation mode to isolate the primary drivers of delays.
[29] Provide actionable recommendations supported by data. Each recommendation should include an estimated impact (cost savings, service improvement, or capacity optimization) and an implementation priority ranking.

[{"content": "[0] NOVATRANS LOGISTICS
[1] Delivering Excellence Across Every Mile
[3] INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
[5] DATE:  January 15, 2024
[6] TO:  Operations Consulting Team
[7] FROM:  David Chen, Chief Operating Officer, NovaTrans Logistics
[8] SUBJECT:  Engagement Brief: Distribution Network Efficiency Review
[10] 1. Background & Context
[11] NovaTrans Logistics is a mid-sized, port-based logistics company specializing in freight distribution and supply chain fulfillment. We currently operate 19 distribution plants strategically positioned across our network, handling the movement of goods between manufacturing origins, inland warehouses, and port terminals.
[12] On an annual basis, our network processes roughly 9,000+ individual shipments spanning multiple transportation modes, including SEA, AIR, and ROAD. We serve a diverse portfolio of customers under three distinct service levels:
[13] CRF (Cross-dock Freight) -- Goods are consolidated at a cross-dock facility and forwarded without long-term storage, optimizing transit speed.
[14] DTD (Door-to-Door) -- Full end-to-end delivery from origin to the customer's designated receiving location.
[15] DTP (Door-to-Port) -- Delivery from the origin point to the designated port terminal, where the customer or a third-party forwarder assumes custody.
[16] Our ERP system captures detailed transactional data for every order, including origin/destination plant codes, shipment dates, carrier assignments, freight costs, and warehouse throughput metrics. This data forms the foundation for the analysis we are requesting.
[17] 2. Problem Statement
[18] Despite steady revenue growth over the past three fiscal years, our operating margins have come under increasing pressure. Preliminary internal reviews point to several areas of concern that require rigorous, data-driven investigation:
[19] Rising Freight Costs. Overall freight expenditure has increased disproportionately relative to shipment volume. The AIR transportation mode, in particular, exhibits significantly higher per-unit costs compared to SEA and ROAD, yet continues to be utilized for shipments where alternative modes may be viable. We need a clear understanding of cost drivers across carriers and routes.
[20] Late Shipments & Customer Dissatisfaction. Approximately 2% of all orders ship late relative to their scheduled ship date. While this figure may appear modest, it translates to a meaningful number of affected customers each quarter, eroding satisfaction and jeopardizing key accounts. Our Q4 2023 customer satisfaction survey data reinforces this concern.
[21] Uneven Warehouse Utilization. Warehouse throughput varies dramatically across our plant network. For example, PLANT01 handles approximately 1,070 units per day, making it one of our highest-volume facilities, while PLANT15 processes only around 11 units per day. This imbalance raises questions about capacity allocation, fixed cost absorption, and whether certain low-volume plants should be consolidated or repurposed.
[22] Carrier & Route Cost Variability. We suspect that significant cost-efficiency differences exist between carrier-route combinations. Some carriers may deliver comparable service levels at materially lower rates on specific lanes, but we lack a consolidated view to validate this hypothesis and act on it.
[23] 3. Scope of Engagement
[24] We are engaging your team to conduct a comprehensive review of our distribution network operations. Specifically, we request that you:
[25] Analyze the order and shipment data to identify operational bottlenecks, including transit-time outliers, mode-selection inefficiencies, and demand concentration patterns.
[26] Evaluate freight cost efficiency across carriers, transportation modes, and specific origin-destination routes. Identify lanes where cost savings are achievable without degrading service quality.
[27] Assess warehouse capacity utilization across all 19 plants. Determine which facilities are over- or under-utilized relative to their stated capacity and recommend rebalancing strategies.
[28] Identify root causes of late shipments. Correlate late-shipment data with plant origin, carrier assignment, service level, and transportation mode to isolate the primary drivers of delays.
[29] Provide actionable recommendations supported by data. Each recommendation should include an estimated impact (cost savings, service improvement, or capacity optimization) and an implementation priority ranking.
[30] 4. Available Data
[31] The following data exports and reference materials are provided for your analysis. Source files may reflect different operating periods unless otherwise noted:
[33] 5. Expected Deliverables
[34] Upon completion of the engagement, we expect the following deliverables:
[35] Excel-Based Analysis Workbook. A comprehensive workbook containing separate tabs for each analytical dimension (freight cost analysis, warehouse utilization, late shipment analysis, carrier/route comparison, etc.). Each tab should include source data summaries, pivot analyses, charts where appropriate, and key findings highlighted in a consistent format.
[36] Executive Summary Report (Word Document). A standalone Word document (maximum 10 pages) summarizing the engagement findings, key insights, and prioritized recommendations. This document will be circulated to the executive leadership team and should be written at a level appropriate for a C-suite audience. Include an executive summary on the first page, followed by detailed sections for each analytical area, and conclude with a prioritized action plan.
[37] 6. Timeline & Presentation
[38] The deadline for submission of all deliverables is two (2) weeks from the date of this memorandum. Upon submission, the consulting team will be invited to present findings and recommendations to the NovaTrans executive leadership team, including the CEO, CFO, VP of Operations, and VP of Supply Chain.
[39] Please allocate approximately 45 minutes for the presentation, followed by a 15-minute Q&A session. Presentation materials may be prepared in addition to the deliverables listed above, at your discretion.
[40] 7. Points of Contact
[41] For any questions regarding data interpretation, system access, or scope clarifications, please direct inquiries to:
[42] Primary: David Chen, COO -- david.chen@novatrans-logistics.com
[43] Secondary: Maria Santos, Director of Operations -- maria.santos@novatrans-logistics.com
[44] Data/IT: James Park, Senior Data Analyst -- james.park@novatrans-logistics.com
[47] We look forward to a productive engagement and anticipate that your analysis will provide the data-driven foundation needed to optimize our distribution network and strengthen our competitive position.
[49] Regards,
[51] David Chen
[52] Chief Operating Officer

Wait — this is the classic "supply chain logistics problem" dataset from Brunel. The OrderList only includes plants connected to PORT09 (dest). [13] CRF (Cross-dock Freight) -- Goods are consolidated at a cross-dock facility and forwarded without long-term storage, optimizing transit speed.
[14] DTD (Door-to-Door) -- Full end-to-end delivery from origin to the customer's designated receiving location.
[15] DTP (Door-to-Port) -- Delivery from the origin point to the designated port terminal, where the customer or a third-party forwarder assumes custody.
[16] Our ERP system captures detailed transactional data for every order, including origin/destination plant codes, shipment dates, carrier assignments, freight costs, and warehouse throughput metrics. This data forms the foundation for the analysis we are requesting.
[17] 2. Problem Statement

[21] Uneven Warehouse Utilization. Warehouse throughput varies dramatically across our plant network. For example, PLANT01 handles approximately 1,070 units per day, making it one of our highest-volume facilities, while PLANT15 processes only around 11 units per day. [28] Identify root causes of late shipments. Correlate late-shipment data with plant origin, carrier assignment, service level, and transportation mode to isolate the primary drivers of delays.

[12] On an annual basis, our network processes roughly 9,000+ individual shipments spanning multiple transportation modes, including SEA, AIR, and ROAD. We serve a diverse portfolio of customers under three distinct service levels:
[13] CRF (Cross-dock Freight) -- Goods are consolidated at a cross-dock facility and forwarded without long-term storage, optimizing transit speed.
[14] DTD (Door-to-Door) -- Full end-to-end delivery from origin to the customer's designated receiving location.
[15] DTP (Door-to-Port) -- Delivery from the origin point to the designated port terminal, where the customer or a third-party forwarder assumes custody.
[16] Our ERP system captures detailed transactional data for every order, including origin/destination plant codes, shipment dates, carrier assignments, freight costs, and warehouse throughput metrics. This data forms the foundation for the analysis we are requesting.
[17] 2. Problem Statement
[18] Despite steady revenue growth over the past three fiscal years, our operating margins have come under increasing pressure. Preliminary internal reviews point to several areas of concern that require rigorous, data-driven investigation:
[19] Rising Freight Costs. Overall freight expenditure has increased disproportionately relative to shipment volume. The AIR transportation mode, in particular, exhibits significantly higher per-unit costs compared to SEA and ROAD, yet continues to be utilized for shipments where alternative modes may be viable. We need a clear understanding of cost drivers across carriers and routes.
[20] Late Shipments & Customer Dissatisfaction. Approximately 2% of all orders ship late relative to their scheduled ship date. While this figure may appear modest, it translates to a meaningful number of affected customers each quarter, eroding satisfaction and jeopardizing key accounts. Our Q4 2023 customer satisfaction survey data reinforces this concern.
[21] Uneven Warehouse Utilization. Warehouse throughput varies dramatically across our plant network. For example, PLANT01 handles approximately 1,070 units per day, making it one of our highest-volume facilities, while PLANT15 processes only around 11 units per day. This imbalance raises questions about capacity allocation, fixed cost absorption, and whether certain low-volume plants should be consolidated or repurposed.
[22] Carrier & Route Cost Variability. We suspect that significant cost-efficiency differences exist between carrier-route combinations. Some carriers may deliver comparable service levels at materially lower rates on specific lanes, but we lack a consolidated view to validate this hypothesis and act on it.
[23] 3. Scope of Engagement
[24] We are engaging your team to conduct a comprehensive review of our distribution network operations. Specifically, we request that you:
[25] Analyze the order and shipment data to identify operational bottlenecks, including transit-time outliers, mode-selection inefficiencies, and demand concentration patterns.
[26] Evaluate freight cost efficiency across carriers, transportation modes, and specific origin-destination routes. Identify lanes where cost savings are achievable without degrading service quality.
[27] Assess warehouse capacity utilization across all 19 plants. Determine which facilities are over- or under-utilized relative to their stated capacity and recommend rebalancing strategies.
[28] Identify root causes of late shipments. Correlate late-shipment data with plant origin, carrier assignment, service level, and transportation mode to isolate the primary drivers of delays.
[29] Provide actionable recommendations supported by data. Each recommendation should include an estimated impact (cost savings, service improvement, or capacity optimization) and an implementation priority ranking.

Next, deep dive into OrderList.csv and FreightRates.csv to build the analysis. Let me set up a comprehensive analysis script.

Key analyses needed:
1. Per-plant volume (units, orders) from OrderList
2. Late shipment rate overall and by plant (Ship_Late_Day_Count > 0)
3. Mode usage by plant (AIR share)
4. PlantPorts topology — which plants share ports; port access for redistribution
5. WhCapacities & WhCosts — cost per unit, utilization
6. FreightRates — carrier rates per lane/mode/weight slab
7. Complaint data by plant
8. Survey scores by plant

Composite scoring model dimensions (operationalizing "structurally unviable"):
- Volume scale (orders/units handled — low volume = weak fixed-cost absorption)
- Warehouse utilization (throughput vs capacity)
- Cost per unit (WhCosts)
- Service quality (late rate, complaints, satisfaction)
- Network redundancy (does the plant share its port(s) with other plants? If its port is unique, closing it may strand volume; if shared, volume can be absorbed)
- Cost efficiency of freight from its port

Let me define structurally unviable: a plant that combines (a) minimal scale relative to fixed cost absorption, (b) high unit handling cost or under-utilized capacity, (c) weak service performance, and (d) volume that can be feasibly absorbed by network peers (port overlap / capacity headroom).

Let me now run the analysis.

2. Analyze FreightRates (rates by lane/port pairs)

[3] INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
[5] DATE:  January 15, 2024
[6] TO:  Operations Consulting Team
[7] FROM:  David Chen, Chief Operating Officer, NovaTrans Logistics
[8] SUBJECT:  Engagement Brief: Distribution Network Efficiency Review
[10] 1. Background & Context
[11] NovaTrans Logistics is a mid-sized, port-based logistics company specializing in freight distribution and supply chain fulfillment. We currently operate 19 distribution plants strategically positioned across our network, handling the movement of goods between manufacturing origins, inland warehouses, and port terminals.
[12] On an annual basis, our network processes roughly 9,000+ individual shipments spanning multiple transportation modes, including SEA, AIR, and ROAD. We serve a diverse portfolio of customers under three distinct service levels:
[13] CRF (Cross-dock Freight) -- Goods are consolidated at a cross-dock facility and forwarded without long-term storage, optimizing transit speed.
[14] DTD (Door-to-Door) -- Full end-to-end delivery from origin to the customer's designated receiving location.
[15] DTP (Door-to-Port) -- Delivery from the origin point to the designated port terminal, where the customer or a third-party forwarder assumes custody.
[16] Our ERP system captures detailed transactional data for every order, including origin/destination plant codes, shipment dates, carrier assignments, freight costs, and warehouse throughput metrics. This data forms the foundation for the analysis we are requesting.
[17] 2. Problem Statement
[18] Despite steady revenue growth over the past three fiscal years, our operating margins have come under increasing pressure. Preliminary internal reviews point to several areas of concern that require rigorous, data-driven investigation:
[19] Rising Freight Costs. Overall freight expenditure has increased disproportionately relative to shipment volume. The AIR transportation mode, in particular, exhibits significantly higher per-unit costs compared to SEA and ROAD, yet continues to be utilized for shipments where alternative modes may be viable. We need a clear understanding of cost drivers across carriers and routes.
[20] Late Shipments & Customer Dissatisfaction. Approximately 2% of all orders ship late relative to their scheduled ship date. While this figure may appear modest, it translates to a meaningful number of affected customers each quarter, eroding satisfaction and jeopardizing key accounts. Our Q4 2023 customer satisfaction survey data reinforces this concern.
[21] Uneven Warehouse Utilization. Warehouse throughput varies dramatically across our plant network. For example, PLANT01 handles approximately 1,070 units per day, making it one of our highest-volume facilities, while PLANT15 processes only around 11 units per day. This imbalance raises questions about capacity allocation, fixed cost absorption, and whether certain low-volume plants should be consolidated or repurposed.
[22] Carrier & Route Cost Variability. We suspect that significant cost-efficiency differences exist between carrier-route combinations. Some carriers may deliver comparable service levels at materially lower rates on specific lanes, but we lack a consolidated view to validate this hypothesis and act on it.
[23] 3. Scope of Engagement
[24] We are engaging your team to conduct a comprehensive review of our distribution network operations. Specifically, we request that you:
[25] Analyze the order and shipment data to identify operational bottlenecks, including transit-time outliers, mode-selection inefficiencies, and demand concentration patterns.
[26] Evaluate freight cost efficiency across carriers, transportation modes, and specific origin-destination routes. Identify lanes where cost savings are achievable without degrading service quality.
[27] Assess warehouse capacity utilization across all 19 plants. Determine which facilities are over- or under-utilized relative to their stated capacity and recommend rebalancing strategies.
[28] Identify root causes of late shipments. Correlate late-shipment data with plant origin, carrier assignment, service level, and transportation mode to isolate the primary drivers of delays.
[29] Provide actionable recommendations supported by data. Each recommendation should include an estimated impact (cost savings, service improvement, or capacity optimization) and an implementation priority ranking.
[30] 4. Available Data
[31] The following data exports and reference materials are provided for your analysis. Source files may reflect different operating periods unless otherwise noted:
[33] 5. Expected Deliverables
[34] Upon completion of the engagement, we expect the following deliverables:
[35] Excel-Based Analysis Workbook. A comprehensive workbook containing separate tabs for each analytical dimension (freight cost analysis, warehouse utilization, late shipment analysis, carrier/route comparison, etc.). Each tab should include source data summaries, pivot analyses, charts where appropriate, and key findings highlighted in a consistent format.
[36] Executive Summary Report (Word Document). A standalone Word document (maximum 10 pages) summarizing the engagement findings, key insights, and prioritized recommendations. This document will be circulated to the executive leadership team and should be written at a level appropriate for a C-suite audience. Include an executive summary on the first page, followed by detailed sections for each analytical area, and conclude with a prioritized action plan.
[37] 6. Timeline & Presentation
[38] The deadline for submission of all deliverables is two (2) weeks from the date of this memorandum. Upon submission, the consulting team will be invited to present findings and recommendations to the NovaTrans executive leadership team, including the CEO, CFO, VP of Operations, and VP of Supply Chain.
[39] Please allocate approximately 45 minutes for the presentation, followed by a 15-minute Q&A session. Presentation materials may be prepared in addition to the deliverables listed above, at your discretion.
[40] 7. Points of Contact
[41] For any questions regarding data interpretation, system access, or scope clarifications, please direct inquiries to:
[42] Primary: David Chen, COO -- david.chen@novatrans-logistics.com
[43] Secondary: Maria Santos, Director of Operations -- maria.santos@novatrans-logistics.com

[{"content": "[0] NOVATRANS LOGISTICS
[1] Delivering Excellence Across Every Mile
[3] INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
[5] DATE:  January 15, 2024
[6] TO:  Operations Consulting Team
[7] FROM:  David Chen, Chief Operating Officer, NovaTrans Logistics
[8] SUBJECT:  Engagement Brief: Distribution Network Efficiency Review
[10] 1. Background & Context
[11] NovaTrans Logistics is a mid-sized, port-based logistics company specializing in freight distribution and supply chain fulfillment. We currently operate 19 distribution plants strategically positioned across our network, handling the movement of goods between manufacturing origins, inland warehouses, and port terminals.
[12] On an annual basis, our network processes roughly 9,000+ individual shipments spanning multiple transportation modes, including SEA, AIR, and ROAD. We serve a diverse portfolio of customers under three distinct service levels:
[13] CRF (Cross-dock Freight) -- Goods are consolidated at a cross-dock facility and forwarded without long-term storage, optimizing transit speed.
[14] DTD (Door-to-Door) -- Full end-to-end delivery from origin to the customer's designated receiving location.
[15] DTP (Door-to-Port) -- Delivery from the origin point to the designated port terminal, where the customer or a third-party forwarder assumes custody.
[16] Our ERP system captures detailed transactional data for every order, including origin/destination plant codes, shipment dates, carrier assignments, freight costs, and warehouse throughput metrics. This data forms the foundation for the analysis we are requesting.
[17] 2. Problem Statement
[18] Despite steady revenue growth over the past three fiscal years, our operating margins have come under increasing pressure. Preliminary internal reviews point to several areas of concern that require rigorous, data-driven investigation:
[19] Rising Freight Costs. Overall freight expenditure has increased disproportionately relative to shipment volume. The AIR transportation mode, in particular, exhibits significantly higher per-unit costs compared to SEA and ROAD, yet continues to be utilized for shipments where alternative modes may be viable. We need a clear understanding of cost drivers across carriers and routes.
[20] Late Shipments & Customer Dissatisfaction. Approximately 2% of all orders ship late relative to their scheduled ship date. While this figure may appear modest, it translates to a meaningful number of affected customers each quarter, eroding satisfaction and jeopardizing key accounts. Our Q4 2023 customer satisfaction survey data reinforces this concern.
[21] Uneven Warehouse Utilization. Warehouse throughput varies dramatically across our plant network. For example, PLANT01 handles approximately 1,070 units per day, making it one of our highest-volume facilities, while PLANT15 processes only around 11 units per day. This imbalance raises questions about capacity allocation, fixed cost absorption, and whether certain low-volume plants should be consolidated or repurposed.
[22] Carrier & Route Cost Variability. We suspect that significant cost-efficiency differences exist between carrier-route combinations. Some carriers may deliver comparable service levels at materially lower rates on specific lanes, but we lack a consolidated view to validate this hypothesis and act on it.
[23] 3. Scope of Engagement
[24] We are engaging your team to conduct a comprehensive review of our distribution network operations. Specifically, we request that you:
[25] Analyze the order and shipment data to identify operational bottlenecks, including transit-time outliers, mode-selection inefficiencies, and demand concentration patterns.
[26] Evaluate freight cost efficiency across carriers, transportation modes, and specific origin-destination routes. Identify lanes where cost savings are achievable without degrading service quality.
[27] Assess warehouse capacity utilization across all 19 plants. Determine which facilities are over- or under-utilized relative to their stated capacity and recommend rebalancing strategies.
[28] Identify root causes of late shipments. Correlate late-shipment data with plant origin, carrier assignment, service level, and transportation mode to isolate the primary drivers of delays.
[29] Provide actionable recommendations supported by data. Each recommendation should include an estimated impact (cost savings, service improvement, or capacity optimization) and an implementation priority ranking.
[30] 4. Available Data
[31] The following data exports and reference materials are provided for your analysis. Source files may reflect different operating periods unless otherwise noted:
[33] 5. Expected Deliverables
[34] Upon completion of the engagement, we expect the following deliverables:
[35] Excel-Based Analysis Workbook. A comprehensive workbook containing separate tabs for each analytical dimension (freight cost analysis, warehouse utilization, late shipment analysis, carrier/route comparison, etc.). Each tab should include source data summaries, pivot analyses, charts where appropriate, and key findings highlighted in a consistent format.
[36] Executive Summary Report (Word Document). A standalone Word document (maximum 10 pages) summarizing the engagement findings, key insights, and prioritized recommendations. This document will be circulated to the executive leadership team and should be written at a level appropriate for a C-suite audience. Include an executive summary on the first page, followed by detailed sections for each analytical area, and conclude with a prioritized action plan.
[37] 6. Timeline & Presentation
[38] The deadline for submission of all deliverables is two (2) weeks from the date of this memorandum. Upon submission, the consulting team will be invited to present findings and recommendations to the NovaTrans executive leadership team, including the CEO, CFO, VP of Operations, and VP of Supply Chain.
[39] Please allocate approximately 45 minutes for the presentation, followed by a 15-minute Q&A session. Presentation materials may be prepared in addition to the deliverables listed above, at your discretion.
[40] 7. Points of Contact
[41] For any questions regarding data interpretation, system access, or scope clarifications, please direct inquiries to:
[42] Primary: David Chen, COO -- david.chen@novatrans-logistics.com
[43] Secondary: Maria Santos, Director of Operations -- maria.santos@novatrans-logistics.com
[44] Data/IT: James Park, Senior Data Analyst -- james.park@novatrans-logistics.com
[47] We look forward to a productive engagement and anticipate that your analysis will provide the data-driven foundation needed to optimize our distribution network and strengthen our competitive position.
[49] Regards,
[51] David Chen
[52] Chief Operating Officer
[53] NovaTrans Logistics

[{"content": "[0] NOVATRANS LOGISTICS
[1] Delivering Excellence Across Every Mile
[3] INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
[5] DATE:  January 15, 2024
[6] TO:  Operations Consulting Team
[7] FROM:  David Chen, Chief Operating Officer, NovaTrans Logistics
[8] SUBJECT:  Engagement Brief: Distribution Network Efficiency Review
[10] 1. Background & Context
[11] NovaTrans Logistics is a mid-sized, port-based logistics company specializing in freight distribution and supply chain fulfillment. We currently operate 19 distribution plants strategically positioned across our network, handling the movement of goods between manufacturing origins, inland warehouses, and port terminals.
[12] On an annual basis, our network processes roughly 9,000+ individual shipments spanning multiple transportation modes, including SEA, AIR, and ROAD. We serve a diverse portfolio of customers under three distinct service levels:
[13] CRF (Cross-dock Freight) -- Goods are consolidated at a cross-dock facility and forwarded without long-term storage, optimizing transit speed.
[14] DTD (Door-to-Door) -- Full end-to-end delivery from origin to the customer's designated receiving location.
[15] DTP (Door-to-Port) -- Delivery from the origin point to the designated port terminal, where the customer or a third-party forwarder assumes custody.
[16] Our ERP system captures detailed transactional data for every order, including origin/destination plant codes, shipment dates, carrier assignments, freight costs, and warehouse throughput metrics. This data forms the foundation for the analysis we are requesting.
[17] 2. Problem Statement
[18] Despite steady revenue growth over the past three fiscal years, our operating margins have come under increasing pressure. Preliminary internal reviews point to several areas of concern that require rigorous, data-driven investigation:
[19] Rising Freight Costs. Overall freight expenditure has increased disproportionately relative to shipment volume. The AIR transportation mode, in particular, exhibits significantly higher per-unit costs compared to SEA and ROAD, yet continues to be utilized for shipments where alternative modes may be viable. We need a clear understanding of cost drivers across carriers and routes.
[20] Late Shipments & Customer Dissatisfaction. Approximately 2% of all orders ship late relative to their scheduled ship date. While this figure may appear modest, it translates to a meaningful number of affected customers each quarter, eroding satisfaction and jeopardizing key accounts. Our Q4 2023 customer satisfaction survey data reinforces this concern.
[21] Uneven Warehouse Utilization. Warehouse throughput varies dramatically across our plant network. For example, PLANT01 handles approximately 1,070 units per day, making it one of our highest-volume facilities, while PLANT15 processes only around 11 units per day. This imbalance raises questions about capacity allocation, fixed cost absorption, and whether certain low-volume plants should be consolidated or repurposed.
[22] Carrier & Route Cost Variability. We suspect that significant cost-efficiency differences exist between carrier-route combinations. Some carriers may deliver comparable service levels at materially lower rates on specific lanes, but we lack a consolidated view to validate this hypothesis and act on it.
[23] 3. Scope of Engagement
[24] We are engaging your team to conduct a comprehensive review of our distribution network operations. Specifically, we request that you:
[25] Analyze the order and shipment data to identify operational bottlenecks, including transit-time outliers, mode-selection inefficiencies, and demand concentration patterns.
[26] Evaluate freight cost efficiency across carriers, transportation modes, and specific origin-destination routes. Identify lanes where cost savings are achievable without degrading service quality.
[27] Assess warehouse capacity utilization across all 19 plants. Determine which facilities are over- or under-utilized relative to their stated capacity and recommend rebalancing strategies.
[28] Identify root causes of late shipments. Correlate late-shipment data with plant origin, carrier assignment, service level, and transportation mode to isolate the primary drivers of delays.
[29] Provide actionable recommendations supported by data. Each recommendation should include an estimated impact (cost savings, service improvement, or capacity optimization) and an implementation priority ranking.
[30] 4. Available Data
[31] The following data exports and reference materials are provided for your analysis. Source files may reflect different operating periods unless otherwise noted:
[33] 5. Expected Deliverables
[34] Upon completion of the engagement, we expect the following deliverables:
[35] Excel-Based Analysis Workbook. A comprehensive workbook containing separate tabs for each analytical dimension (freight cost analysis, warehouse utilization, late shipment analysis, carrier/route comparison, etc.). Each tab should include source data summaries, pivot analyses, charts where appropriate, and key findings highlighted in a consistent format.
[36] Executive Summary Report (Word Document). A standalone Word document (maximum 10 pages) summarizing the engagement findings, key insights, and prioritized recommendations. This document will be circulated to the executive leadership team and should be written at a level appropriate for a C-suite audience. Include an executive summary on the first page, followed by detailed sections for each analytical area, and conclude with a prioritized action plan.
[37] 6. Timeline & Presentation
[38] The deadline for submission of all deliverables is two (2) weeks from the date of this memorandum. Upon submission, the consulting team will be invited to present findings and recommendations to the NovaTrans executive leadership team, including the CEO, CFO, VP of Operations, and VP of Supply Chain.
[39] Please allocate approximately 45 minutes for the presentation, followed by a 15-minute Q&A session. Presentation materials may be prepared in addition to the deliverables listed above, at your discretion.
[40] 7. Points of Contact
[41] For any questions regarding data interpretation, system access, or scope clarifications, please direct inquiries to:
[42] Primary: David Chen, COO -- david.chen@novatrans-logistics.com
[43] Secondary: Maria Santos, Director of Operations -- maria.santos@novatrans-logistics.com
[44] Data/IT: James Park, Senior Data Analyst -- james.park@novatrans-logistics.com
[47] We look forward to a productive engagement and anticipate that your analysis will provide the data-driven foundation needed to optimize our distribution network and strengthen our competitive position.
[49] Regards,
[51] David Chen
[52] Chief Operating Officer
[53] NovaTrans Logistics
