I should present this as a reconciliation finding rather than trying to force utilization = units/capacity.

Let me design the composite score with available data for ALL 19 plants, using indicators that exist network-wide, plus order-derived indicators for the 7 covered plants (flagged as observed vs stated).

Proposed weighted model (0–100 scale, higher = stronger consolidation candidate):

1. **Capacity Scale Score (25%)** — stated daily capacity. Smaller capacity → weaker fixed-cost absorption → higher candidacy. Rationale: a plant whose stated capacity is a trivial share of network capacity cannot absorb fixed costs; the memo itself flags the capacity imbalance (PLANT01 1,070 vs PLANT15 11).
   Normalize: score = 100 × (1 - rank percentile) or scaled inverse.

[{"content": "[0] NOVATRANS LOGISTICS
[1] Delivering Excellence Across Every Mile
[3] INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
[5] DATE:  January 15, 2024
[6] TO:  Operations Consulting Team
[7] FROM:  David Chen, Chief Operating Officer, NovaTrans Logistics
[8] SUBJECT:  Engagement Brief: Distribution Network Efficiency Review
[10] 1. Background & Context
[11] NovaTrans Logistics is a mid-sized, port-based logistics company specializing in freight distribution and supply chain fulfillment. We currently operate 19 distribution plants strategically positioned across our network, handling the movement of goods between manufacturing origins, inland warehouses, and port terminals.
[12] On an annual basis, our network processes roughly 9,000+ individual shipments spanning multiple transportation modes, including SEA, AIR, and ROAD. We serve a diverse portfolio of customers under three distinct service levels:
[13] CRF (Cross-dock Freight) -- Goods are consolidated at a cross-dock facility and forwarded without long-term storage, optimizing transit speed.
[14] DTD (Door-to-Door) -- Full end-to-end delivery from origin to the customer's designated receiving location.
[15] DTP (Door-to-Port) -- Delivery from the origin point to the designated port terminal, where the customer or a third-party forwarder assumes custody.
[16] Our ERP system captures detailed transactional data for every order, including origin/destination plant codes, shipment dates, carrier assignments, freight costs, and warehouse throughput metrics. This data forms the foundation for the analysis we are requesting.
[17] 2. Problem Statement
[18] Despite steady revenue growth over the past three fiscal years, our operating margins have come under increasing pressure. Preliminary internal reviews point to several areas of concern that require rigorous, data-driven investigation:
[19] Rising Freight Costs. Overall freight expenditure has increased disproportionately relative to shipment volume. The AIR transportation mode, in particular, exhibits significantly higher per-unit costs compared to SEA and ROAD, yet continues to be utilized for shipments where alternative modes may be viable. We need a clear understanding of cost drivers across carriers and routes.
[20] Late Shipments & Customer Dissatisfaction. Approximately 2% of all orders ship late relative to their scheduled ship date. While this figure may appear modest, it translates to a meaningful number of affected customers each quarter, eroding satisfaction and jeopardizing key accounts. Our Q4 2023 customer satisfaction survey data reinforces this concern.
[21] Uneven Warehouse Utilization. Warehouse throughput varies dramatically across our plant network. For example, PLANT01 handles approximately 1,070 units per day, making it one of our highest-volume facilities, while PLANT15 processes only around 11 units per day. This imbalance raises questions about capacity allocation, fixed cost absorption, and whether certain low-volume plants should be consolidated or repurposed.
[22] Carrier & Route Cost Variability. We suspect that significant cost-efficiency differences exist between carrier-route combinations. Some carriers may deliver comparable service levels at materially lower rates on specific lanes, but we lack a consolidated view to validate this hypothesis and act on it.
[23] 3. Scope of Engagement
[24] We are engaging your team to conduct a comprehensive review of our distribution network operations. Specifically, we request that you:
[25] Analyze the order and shipment data to identify operational bottlenecks, including transit-time outliers, mode-selection inefficiencies, and demand concentration patterns.
[26] Evaluate freight cost efficiency across carriers, transportation modes, and specific origin-destination routes. Identify lanes where cost savings are achievable without degrading service quality.
[27] Assess warehouse capacity utilization across all 19 plants. Determine which facilities are over- or under-utilized relative to their stated capacity and recommend rebalancing strategies.
[28] Identify root causes of late shipments. Correlate late-shipment data with plant origin, carrier assignment, service level, and transportation mode to isolate the primary drivers of delays.
[29] Provide actionable recommendations supported by data. Each recommendation should include an estimated impact (cost savings, service improvement, or capacity optimization) and an implementation priority ranking.
[30] 4. Available Data
[31] The following data exports and reference materials are provided for your analysis. Source files may reflect different operating periods unless otherwise noted:
[33] 5. Expected Deliverables
[34] Upon completion of the engagement, we expect the following deliverables:
[35] Excel-Based Analysis Workbook. A comprehensive workbook containing separate tabs for each analytical dimension (freight cost analysis, warehouse utilization, late shipment analysis, carrier/route comparison, etc.). Each tab should include source data summaries, pivot analyses, charts where appropriate, and key findings highlighted in a consistent format.
[36] Executive Summary Report (Word Document). A standalone Word document (maximum 10 pages) summarizing the engagement findings, key insights, and prioritized recommendations. This document will be circulated to the executive leadership team and should be written at a level appropriate for a C-suite audience. Include an executive summary on the first page, followed by detailed sections for each analytical area, and conclude with a prioritized action plan.
[37] 6. Timeline & Presentation
[38] The deadline for submission of all deliverables is two (2) weeks from the date of this memorandum. Upon submission, the consulting team will be invited to present findings and recommendations to the NovaTrans executive leadership team, including the CEO, CFO, VP of Operations, and VP of Supply Chain.
[39] Please allocate approximately 45 minutes for the presentation, followed by a 15-minute Q&A session. Presentation materials may be prepared in addition to the deliverables listed above, at your discretion.
[40] 7. Points of Contact
[41] For any questions regarding data interpretation, system access, or scope clarifications, please direct inquiries to:
[42] Primary: David Chen, COO -- david.chen@novatrans-logistics.com
[43] Secondary: Maria Santos, Director of Operations -- maria.santos@novatrans-logistics.com
[44] Data/IT: James Park, Senior Data Analyst -- james.park@novatrans-logistics.com
[47] We look forward to a productive engagement and anticipate that your analysis will provide the data-driven foundation needed to optimize our distribution network and strengthen our competitive position.
[49] Regards,
[51] David Chen
[52] Chief Operating Officer
[53] NovaTrans Logistics

[8] SUBJECT:  Engagement Brief: Distribution Network Efficiency Review
[10] 1. Background & Context
[11] NovaTrans Logistics is a mid-sized, port-based logistics company specializing in freight distribution and supply chain fulfillment. We currently operate 19 distribution plants strategically positioned across our network, handling the movement of goods between manufacturing origins, inland warehouses, and port terminals.
[12] On an annual basis, our network processes roughly 9,000+ individual shipments spanning multiple transportation modes, including SEA, AIR, and ROAD. We serve a diverse portfolio of customers under three distinct service levels:
[13] CRF (Cross-dock Freight) -- Goods are consolidated at a cross-dock facility and forwarded without long-term storage, optimizing transit speed.
[14] DTD (Door-to-Door) -- Full end-to-end delivery from origin to the customer's designated receiving location.
[15] DTP (Door-to-Port) -- Delivery from the origin point to the designated port terminal, where the customer or a third-party forwarder assumes custody.
[16] Our ERP system captures detailed transactional data for every order, including origin/destination plant codes, shipment dates, carrier assignments, freight costs, and warehouse throughput metrics. This data forms the foundation for the analysis we are requesting.
[17] 2. Problem Statement
[18] Despite steady revenue growth over the past three fiscal years, our operating margins have come under increasing pressure. Preliminary internal reviews point to several areas of concern that require rigorous, data-driven investigation:
[19] Rising Freight Costs. Overall freight expenditure has increased disproportionately relative to shipment volume. The AIR transportation mode, in particular, exhibits significantly higher per-unit costs compared to SEA and ROAD, yet continues to be utilized for shipments where alternative modes may be viable. We need a clear understanding of cost drivers across carriers and routes.
[20] Late Shipments & Customer Dissatisfaction. Approximately 2% of all orders ship late relative to their scheduled ship date. While this figure may appear modest, it translates to a meaningful number of affected customers each quarter, eroding satisfaction and jeopardizing key accounts. Our Q4 2023 customer satisfaction survey data reinforces this concern.
[21] Uneven Warehouse Utilization. Warehouse throughput varies dramatically across our plant network. For example, PLANT01 handles approximately 1,070 units per day, making it one of our highest-volume facilities, while PLANT15 processes only around 11 units per day. This imbalance raises questions about capacity allocation, fixed cost absorption, and whether certain low-volume plants should be consolidated or repurposed.
[22] Carrier & Route Cost Variability. We suspect that significant cost-efficiency differences exist between carrier-route combinations. Some carriers may deliver comparable service levels at materially lower rates on specific lanes, but we lack a consolidated view to validate this hypothesis and act on it.
[23] 3. Scope of Engagement
[24] We are engaging your team to conduct a comprehensive review of our distribution network operations. Specifically, we request that you:
[25] Analyze the order and shipment data to identify operational bottlenecks, including transit-time outliers, mode-selection inefficiencies, and demand concentration patterns.
[26] Evaluate freight cost efficiency across carriers, transportation modes, and specific origin-destination routes. Identify lanes where cost savings are achievable without degrading service quality.
[27] Assess warehouse capacity utilization across all 19 plants. Determine which facilities are over- or under-utilized relative to their stated capacity and recommend rebalancing strategies.
[28] Identify root causes of late shipments. Correlate late-shipment data with plant origin, carrier assignment, service level, and transportation mode to isolate the primary drivers of delays.
[29] Provide actionable recommendations supported by data. Each recommendation should include an estimated impact (cost savings, service improvement, or capacity optimization) and an implementation priority ranking.

[{"content": "[0] NOVATRANS LOGISTICS
[1] Delivering Excellence Across Every Mile
[3] INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
[5] DATE:  January 15, 2024
[6] TO:  Operations Consulting Team
[7] FROM:  David Chen, Chief Operating Officer, NovaTrans Logistics
[8] SUBJECT:  Engagement Brief: Distribution Network Efficiency Review
[10] 1. Background & Context
[11] NovaTrans Logistics is a mid-sized, port-based logistics company specializing in freight distribution and supply chain fulfillment. We currently operate 19 distribution plants strategically positioned across our network, handling the movement of goods between manufacturing origins, inland warehouses, and port terminals.
[12] On an annual basis, our network processes roughly 9,000+ individual shipments spanning multiple transportation modes, including SEA, AIR, and ROAD. We serve a diverse portfolio of customers under three distinct service levels:
[13] CRF (Cross-dock Freight) -- Goods are consolidated at a cross-dock facility and forwarded without long-term storage, optimizing transit speed.
[14] DTD (Door-to-Door) -- Full end-to-end delivery from origin to the customer's designated receiving location.
[15] DTP (Door-to-Port) -- Delivery from the origin point to the designated port terminal, where the customer or a third-party forwarder assumes custody.
[16] Our ERP system captures detailed transactional data for every order, including origin/destination plant codes, shipment dates, carrier assignments, freight costs, and warehouse throughput metrics. This data forms the foundation for the analysis we are requesting.
[17] 2. Problem Statement
[18] Despite steady revenue growth over the past three fiscal years, our operating margins have come under increasing pressure. Preliminary internal reviews point to several areas of concern that require rigorous, data-driven investigation:
[19] Rising Freight Costs. Overall freight expenditure has increased disproportionately relative to shipment volume. The AIR transportation mode, in particular, exhibits significantly higher per-unit costs compared to SEA and ROAD, yet continues to be utilized for shipments where alternative modes may be viable. We need a clear understanding of cost drivers across carriers and routes.
[20] Late Shipments & Customer Dissatisfaction. Approximately 2% of all orders ship late relative to their scheduled ship date. While this figure may appear modest, it translates to a meaningful number of affected customers each quarter, eroding satisfaction and jeopardizing key accounts. Our Q4 2023 customer satisfaction survey data reinforces this concern.
[21] Uneven Warehouse Utilization. Warehouse throughput varies dramatically across our plant network. For example, PLANT01 handles approximately 1,070 units per day, making it one of our highest-volume facilities, while PLANT15 processes only around 11 units per day. This imbalance raises questions about capacity allocation, fixed cost absorption, and whether certain low-volume plants should be consolidated or repurposed.
[22] Carrier & Route Cost Variability. We suspect that significant cost-efficiency differences exist between carrier-route combinations. Some carriers may deliver comparable service levels at materially lower rates on specific lanes, but we lack a consolidated view to validate this hypothesis and act on it.
[23] 3. Scope of Engagement
[24] We are engaging your team to conduct a comprehensive review of our distribution network operations. Specifically, we request that you:
[25] Analyze the order and shipment data to identify operational bottlenecks, including transit-time outliers, mode-selection inefficiencies, and demand concentration patterns.
[26] Evaluate freight cost efficiency across carriers, transportation modes, and specific origin-destination routes. Identify lanes where cost savings are achievable without degrading service quality.
[27] Assess warehouse capacity utilization across all 19 plants. Determine which facilities are over- or under-utilized relative to their stated capacity and recommend rebalancing strategies.
[28] Identify root causes of late shipments. Correlate late-shipment data with plant origin, carrier assignment, service level, and transportation mode to isolate the primary drivers of delays.
[29] Provide actionable recommendations supported by data. Each recommendation should include an estimated impact (cost savings, service improvement, or capacity optimization) and an implementation priority ranking.
[30] 4. Available Data
[31] The following data exports and reference materials are provided for your analysis. Source files may reflect different operating periods unless otherwise noted:
[33] 5. Expected Deliverables
[34] Upon completion of the engagement, we expect the following deliverables:
[35] Excel-Based Analysis Workbook. A comprehensive workbook containing separate tabs for each analytical dimension (freight cost analysis, warehouse utilization, late shipment analysis, carrier/route comparison, etc.). Each tab should include source data summaries, pivot analyses, charts where appropriate, and key findings highlighted in a consistent format.
[36] Executive Summary Report (Word Document). A standalone Word document (maximum 10 pages) summarizing the engagement findings, key insights, and prioritized recommendations. This document will be circulated to the executive leadership team and should be written at a level appropriate for a C-suite audience. Include an executive summary on the first page, followed by detailed sections for each analytical area, and conclude with a prioritized action plan.
[37] 6. Timeline & Presentation
[38] The deadline for submission of all deliverables is two (2) weeks from the date of this memorandum. Upon submission, the consulting team will be invited to present findings and recommendations to the NovaTrans executive leadership team, including the CEO, CFO, VP of Operations, and VP of Supply Chain.
[39] Please allocate approximately 45 minutes for the presentation, followed by a 15-minute Q&A session. Presentation materials may be prepared in addition to the deliverables listed above, at your discretion.
[40] 7. Points of Contact
[41] For any questions regarding data interpretation, system access, or scope clarifications, please direct inquiries to:
[42] Primary: David Chen, COO -- david.chen@novatrans-logistics.com
[43] Secondary: Maria Santos, Director of Operations -- maria.santos@novatrans-logistics.com
[44] Data/IT: James Park, Senior Data Analyst -- james.park@novatrans-logistics.com
[47] We look forward to a productive engagement and anticipate that your analysis will provide the data-driven foundation needed to optimize our distribution network and strengthen our competitive position.
[49] Regards,
[51] David Chen
[52] Chief Operating Officer
[53] NovaTrans Logistics
[55] CONFIDENTIAL -- This memorandum and all accompanying data files are the property of NovaTrans Logistics and are intended solely for the use of the designated consulting team. Unauthorized distribution is prohibited.

[17] 2. Problem Statement
[18] Despite steady revenue growth over the past three fiscal years, our operating margins have come under increasing pressure. Preliminary internal reviews point to several areas of concern that require rigorous, data-driven investigation:
[19] Rising Freight Costs. Overall freight expenditure has increased disproportionately relative to shipment volume. The AIR transportation mode, in particular, exhibits significantly higher per-unit costs compared to SEA and ROAD, yet continues to be utilized for shipments where alternative modes may be viable. We need a clear understanding of cost drivers across carriers and routes.
[20] Late Shipments & Customer Dissatisfaction. Approximately 2% of all orders ship late relative to their scheduled ship date. [21] Uneven Warehouse Utilization. Warehouse throughput varies dramatically across our plant network. For example, PLANT01 handles approximately 1,070 units per day, making it one of our highest-volume facilities, while PLANT15 processes only around 11 units per day. This imbalance raises questions about capacity allocation, fixed cost absorption, and whether certain low-volume plants should be consolidated or repurposed.
[22] Carrier & Route Cost Variability. We suspect that significant cost-efficiency differences exist between carrier-route combinations. [{"content": ""You are a Management Analyst consultant engaged by NovaTrans Logistics. The COO has escalated your firm's engagement following a board meeting: NovaTrans is now evaluating a plant consolidation strategy alongside the original efficiency review. Your engagement brief is in \"COO_Engagement_Memo.docx,\" but the board has added a new directive — identify 3–5 candidate plants for closure or consolidation based on a composite scoring model you must design. NovaTrans operates 19 distribution plants, and the board is concerned that some may be structurally unviable. The COO's memo does not define this term — you must operationalize it using the available data.

Your first deliverable is a Plant Consolidation Scoring Model (Excel workbook, .xlsx) with four tabs. The \"Composite_Score\" tab should rank all 19 plants on consolidation candidacy using a weighted model with documented weighting rationale. The \"Consolidation_Scenarios\" tab should model volume redistribution for your top closure candidates, accounting for network topology constraints — port access determines which plants can absorb volume from others — and calculating net cost impact. Source the warehouse capacity data (\"WhCapacities.csv\"), per-unit warehousing cost data (\"WhCosts.csv\"), and carrier rate schedules (\"FreightRates.csv\") from the external Supply Chain Logistics Problem Dataset (Brunel University London, Figshare) referenced in the COO's engagement memo (Section 4: Available Data). The \"Risk_Matrix\" tab should cross-reference complaint data with closure candidates to assess customer attrition risk. The \"Data_Reconciliation\" tab should independently verify key operational claims from the engagement memo against the shipment data and reconcile plant code coverage across all datasets.

Your second deliverable is a Board Decision Brief (Word document, .docx, max 5 pages) containing a Methodology Statement, Consolidation Recommendation with supporting metrics and redistribution plans for each candidate, an Implementation Risk Assessment grounded in specific operational and customer data, and a Go/No-Go Matrix recommending one of three actions per candidate: Close, Consolidate, or Retain-and-Monitor. The COO's memo and the board's directive reflect different strategic priorities — your deliverables should address where these align and where they conflict.

Local Reference Files:
- COO_Engagement_Memo.docx
- Customer_Satisfaction_Survey_Q4.xlsx
- OrderList.csv
- PlantPorts.csv


External reference snapshots are provided in task_folder/references/ when the task requires external sources. Use these pinned files; internet access is unavailable. Write requested deliverables in /work/output/.

[{"content": "[0] NOVATRANS LOGISTICS
[1] Delivering Excellence Across Every Mile
[3] INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
[5] DATE:  January 15, 2024
[6] TO:  Operations Consulting Team
[7] FROM:  David Chen, Chief Operating Officer, NovaTrans Logistics
[8] SUBJECT:  Engagement Brief: Distribution Network Efficiency Review
[10] 1. Background & Context
[11] NovaTrans Logistics is a mid-sized, port-based logistics company specializing in freight distribution and supply chain fulfillment. We currently operate 19 distribution plants strategically positioned across our network, handling the movement of goods between manufacturing origins, inland warehouses, and port terminals.
[12] On an annual basis, our network processes roughly 9,000+ individual shipments spanning multiple transportation modes, including SEA, AIR, and ROAD. We serve a diverse portfolio of customers under three distinct service levels:
[13] CRF (Cross-dock Freight) -- Goods are consolidated at a cross-dock facility and forwarded without long-term storage, optimizing transit speed.
[14] DTD (Door-to-Door) -- Full end-to-end delivery from origin to the customer's designated receiving location.
[15] DTP (Door-to-Port) -- Delivery from the origin point to the designated port terminal, where the customer or a third-party forwarder assumes custody.
[16] Our ERP system captures detailed transactional data for every order, including origin/destination plant codes, shipment dates, carrier assignments, freight costs, and warehouse throughput metrics. This data forms the foundation for the analysis we are requesting.
[17] 2. Problem Statement
[18] Despite steady revenue growth over the past three fiscal years, our operating margins have come under increasing pressure. Preliminary internal reviews point to several areas of concern that require rigorous, data-driven investigation:
[19] Rising Freight Costs. Overall freight expenditure has increased disproportionately relative to shipment volume. The AIR transportation mode, in particular, exhibits significantly higher per-unit costs compared to SEA and ROAD, yet continues to be utilized for shipments where alternative modes may be viable. We need a clear understanding of cost drivers across carriers and routes.
[20] Late Shipments & Customer Dissatisfaction. Approximately 2% of all orders ship late relative to their scheduled ship date. While this figure may appear modest, it translates to a meaningful number of affected customers each quarter, eroding satisfaction and jeopardizing key accounts. Our Q4 2023 customer satisfaction survey data reinforces this concern.
[21] Uneven Warehouse Utilization. Warehouse throughput varies dramatically across our plant network. For example, PLANT01 handles approximately 1,070 units per day, making it one of our highest-volume facilities, while PLANT15 processes only around 11 units per day. This imbalance raises questions about capacity allocation, fixed cost absorption, and whether certain low-volume plants should be consolidated or repurposed.
[22] Carrier & Route Cost Variability. We suspect that significant cost-efficiency differences exist between carrier-route combinations. Some carriers may deliver comparable service levels at materially lower rates on specific lanes, but we lack a consolidated view to validate this hypothesis and act on it.
[23] 3. Scope of Engagement
[24] We are engaging your team to conduct a comprehensive review of our distribution network operations. Specifically, we request that you:
[25] Analyze the order and shipment data to identify operational bottlenecks, including transit-time outliers, mode-selection inefficiencies, and demand concentration patterns.
[26] Evaluate freight cost efficiency across carriers, transportation modes, and specific origin-destination routes. Identify lanes where cost savings are achievable without degrading service quality.
[27] Assess warehouse capacity utilization across all 19 plants. Determine which facilities are over- or under-utilized relative to their stated capacity and recommend rebalancing strategies.
[28] Identify root causes of late shipments. Correlate late-shipment data with plant origin, carrier assignment, service level, and transportation mode to isolate the primary drivers of delays.
[29] Provide actionable recommendations supported by data. Each recommendation should include an estimated impact (cost savings, service improvement, or capacity optimization) and an implementation priority ranking.
[30] 4. Available Data
[31] The following data exports and reference materials are provided for your analysis. Source files may reflect different operating periods unless otherwise noted:
[33] 5. Expected Deliverables
[34] Upon completion of the engagement, we expect the following deliverables:
[35] Excel-Based Analysis Workbook. A comprehensive workbook containing separate tabs for each analytical dimension (freight cost analysis, warehouse utilization, late shipment analysis, carrier/route comparison, etc.). Each tab should include source data summaries, pivot analyses, charts where appropriate, and key findings highlighted in a consistent format.
[36] Executive Summary Report (Word Document). A standalone Word document (maximum 10 pages) summarizing the engagement findings, key insights, and prioritized recommendations. This document will be circulated to the executive leadership team and should be written at a level appropriate for a C-suite audience. Include an executive summary on the first page, followed by detailed sections for each analytical area, and conclude with a prioritized action plan.
[37] 6. Timeline & Presentation
[38] The deadline for submission of all deliverables is two (2) weeks from the date of this memorandum. Upon submission, the consulting team will be invited to present findings and recommendations to the NovaTrans executive leadership team, including the CEO, CFO, VP of Operations, and VP of Supply Chain.
[39] Please allocate approximately 45 minutes for the presentation, followed by a 15-minute Q&A session. Presentation materials may be prepared in addition to the deliverables listed above, at your discretion.
[40] 7. Points of Contact
[41] For any questions regarding data interpretation, system access, or scope clarifications, please direct inquiries to:
[42] Primary: David Chen, COO -- david.chen@novatrans-logistics.com
[43] Secondary: Maria Santos, Director of Operations -- maria.santos@novatrans-logistics.com
[44] Data/IT: James Park, Senior Data Analyst -- james.park@novatrans-logistics.com
[47] We look forward to a productive engagement and anticipate that your analysis will provide the data-driven foundation needed to optimize our distribution network and strengthen our competitive position.
[49] Regards,
[51] David Chen
[52] Chief Operating Officer
[53] NovaTrans Logistics

I should present this as a reconciliation finding rather than trying to force utilization = units/capacity.

Let me design the composite score with available data for ALL 19 plants, using indicators that exist network-wide, plus order-derived indicators for the 7 covered plants (flagged as observed vs stated).

Proposed weighted model (0–100 scale, higher = stronger consolidation candidate):

1. **Capacity Scale Score (25%)** — stated daily capacity. Smaller capacity → weaker fixed-cost absorption → higher candidacy. Rationale: a plant whose stated capacity is a trivial share of network capacity cannot absorb fixed costs; the memo itself flags the capacity imbalance (PLANT01 1,070 vs PLANT15 11).
   Normalize: score = 100 × (1 - rank percentile) or scaled inverse.

[7] FROM:  David Chen, Chief Operating Officer, NovaTrans Logistics
[8] SUBJECT:  Engagement Brief: Distribution Network Efficiency Review
[10] 1. Background & Context
[11] NovaTrans Logistics is a mid-sized, port-based logistics company specializing in freight distribution and supply chain fulfillment. We currently operate 19 distribution plants strategically positioned across our network, handling the movement of goods between manufacturing origins, inland warehouses, and port terminals.
[12] On an annual basis, our network processes roughly 9,000+ individual shipments spanning multiple transportation modes, including SEA, AIR, and ROAD. We serve a diverse portfolio of customers under three distinct service levels:
[13] CRF (Cross-dock Freight) -- Goods are consolidated at a cross-dock facility and forwarded without long-term storage, optimizing transit speed.
[14] DTD (Door-to-Door) -- Full end-to-end delivery from origin to the customer's designated receiving location.
[15] DTP (Door-to-Port) -- Delivery from the origin point to the designated port terminal, where the customer or a third-party forwarder assumes custody.
[16] Our ERP system captures detailed transactional data for every order, including origin/destination plant codes, shipment dates, carrier assignments, freight costs, and warehouse throughput metrics. This data forms the foundation for the analysis we are requesting.
[17] 2. Problem Statement
[18] Despite steady revenue growth over the past three fiscal years, our operating margins have come under increasing pressure. Preliminary internal reviews point to several areas of concern that require rigorous, data-driven investigation:
[19] Rising Freight Costs. Overall freight expenditure has increased disproportionately relative to shipment volume. The AIR transportation mode, in particular, exhibits significantly higher per-unit costs compared to SEA and ROAD, yet continues to be utilized for shipments where alternative modes may be viable. We need a clear understanding of cost drivers across carriers and routes.
[20] Late Shipments & Customer Dissatisfaction. Approximately 2% of all orders ship late relative to their scheduled ship date. While this figure may appear modest, it translates to a meaningful number of affected customers each quarter, eroding satisfaction and jeopardizing key accounts. Our Q4 2023 customer satisfaction survey data reinforces this concern.
[21] Uneven Warehouse Utilization. Warehouse throughput varies dramatically across our plant network. For example, PLANT01 handles approximately 1,070 units per day, making it one of our highest-volume facilities, while PLANT15 processes only around 11 units per day. This imbalance raises questions about capacity allocation, fixed cost absorption, and whether certain low-volume plants should be consolidated or repurposed.
[22] Carrier & Route Cost Variability. We suspect that significant cost-efficiency differences exist between carrier-route combinations. Some carriers may deliver comparable service levels at materially lower rates on specific lanes, but we lack a consolidated view to validate this hypothesis and act on it.
[23] 3. Scope of Engagement
[24] We are engaging your team to conduct a comprehensive review of our distribution network operations. Specifically, we request that you:
[25] Analyze the order and shipment data to identify operational bottlenecks, including transit-time outliers, mode-selection inefficiencies, and demand concentration patterns.
[26] Evaluate freight cost efficiency across carriers, transportation modes, and specific origin-destination routes. Identify lanes where cost savings are achievable without degrading service quality.
[27] Assess warehouse capacity utilization across all 19 plants. Determine which facilities are over- or under-utilized relative to their stated capacity and recommend rebalancing strategies.
[28] Identify root causes of late shipments. Correlate late-shipment data with plant origin, carrier assignment, service level, and transportation mode to isolate the primary drivers of delays.
[29] Provide actionable recommendations supported by data. Each recommendation should include an estimated impact (cost savings, service improvement, or capacity optimization) and an implementation priority ranking.
[30] 4. Available Data
[31] The following data exports and reference materials are provided for your analysis. Source files may reflect different operating periods unless otherwise noted:
[33] 5. Expected Deliverables
[34] Upon completion of the engagement, we expect the following deliverables:
[35] Excel-Based Analysis Workbook. A comprehensive workbook containing separate tabs for each analytical dimension (freight cost analysis, warehouse utilization, late shipment analysis, carrier/route comparison, etc.). Each tab should include source data summaries, pivot analyses, charts where appropriate, and key findings highlighted in a consistent format.
[36] Executive Summary Report (Word Document). A standalone Word document (maximum 10 pages) summarizing the engagement findings, key insights, and prioritized recommendations. This document will be circulated to the executive leadership team and should be written at a level appropriate for a C-suite audience. Include an executive summary on the first page, followed by detailed sections for each analytical area, and conclude with a prioritized action plan.
[37] 6. Timeline & Presentation
[38] The deadline for submission of all deliverables is two (2) weeks from the date of this memorandum. Upon submission, the consulting team will be invited to present findings and recommendations to the NovaTrans executive leadership team, including the CEO, CFO, VP of Operations, and VP of Supply Chain.
[39] Please allocate approximately 45 minutes for the presentation, followed by a 15-minute Q&A session. Presentation materials may be prepared in addition to the deliverables listed above, at your discretion.

{"content": "import pandas as pd, numpy as np, json

orders = pd.read_csv('/work/task_folder/OrderList.csv')
cap = pd.read_csv('/work/task_folder/references/WhCapacities.csv')
cost = pd.read_csv('/work/task_folder/references/WhCosts.csv')
pp = pd.read_csv('/work/task_folder/PlantPorts.csv')
fr = pd.read_csv('/work/task_folder/references/FreightRates.csv')
fr.columns = [c.strip() for c in fr.columns]
fr['Mode_DSC'] = fr['Mode_DSC'].str.strip()
sur = pd.read_excel('/work/task_folder/Customer_Satisfaction_Survey_Q4.xlsx', sheet_name='Survey_Results')
com = pd.read_excel('/work/task_folder/Customer_Satisfaction_Survey_Q4.xlsx', sheet_name='Complaint_Log')

capd = dict(zip(cap.Plant_Code, cap.Daily_Capacity))
costd = dict(zip(cost.Plant_Code, cost.Cost_Per_Unit))
ports = pp.groupby('Plant_Code')['Ports'].apply(list).to_dict()
port_plants = pp.groupby('Ports')['Plant_Code'].apply(list).to_dict()

CAND = ['PLANT19', 'PLANT08', 'PLANT09', 'PLANT15', 'PLANT06']
CLOSING = set(CAND)
TRANSITION_COST = 175000.0

pg = orders.groupby('Plant_Code').agg(orders=('Order_ID', 'count'), units=('Unit_Quant', 'sum'),
    weight=('Weight', 'sum'), customers=('Customer', 'nunique'),
    late=('Ship_Late_Day_Count', lambda s: (s > 0).sum()))
pg['late_rate'] = pg.late / pg.orders

out = {}
for cand in CAND:
    myports = set(ports[cand])
    peers = sorted(set([q for pt in myports for q in port_plants[pt]]) - {cand} - CLOSING)
    peer_cap = {q: capd[q] for q in peers}
    tot_cap = sum(peer_cap.values())
    scen = {'cand': cand, 'unique_port': len(myports) == 1 and all(len(port_plants[pt]) == 1 for pt in myports),
            'peers': peers, 'alloc': {q: round(capd[q] / tot_cap, 4) for q in peers} if tot_cap else {},
            'orders': int(pg.orders.get(cand, 0)), 'units': int(pg.units.get(cand, 0)),
            'weight': float(pg.weight.get(cand, 0)), 'customers': int(pg.customers.get(cand, 0)),
            'late': int(pg.late.get(cand, 0)), 'late_rate': round(float(pg.late_rate.get(cand, 0)), 4),
            'cand_cost': costd[cand]}
    if scen['units'] > 0:
        blend = sum(capd[q] * costd[q] for q in peers) / tot_cap
        scen['blend_peer_cost'] = round(blend, 4)
        scen['d_wh'] = round(scen['units'] * (blend - costd[cand]), 2)
        # peer late-rate blend (order-weighted proxy via allocation shares)
        blend_late = sum((capd[q] / tot_cap) * float(pg.late_rate.get(q, 0.0)) for q in peers)
        scen['blend_peer_late'] = round(blend_late, 4)
        scen['exp_late_after'] = int(round(scen['orders'] * blend_late))
        scen['d_freight'] = 0.0
        scen['freight_note'] = 'Same-port absorption (PORT04 cluster): origin port unchanged -> lane rates unchanged (FreightRates)'
    else:
        scen['d_wh'] = 0.0
        scen['d_freight'] = 0.0
        scen['freight_note'] = 'No observed volume in order book; no freight re-rating required'
    scen['one_off'] = TRANSITION_COST
    scen['net_period'] = round(-(scen['d_wh'] + scen['d_freight']), 2)  # negative = cost increase
    out[cand] = scen

for k, v in out.items():
    print(json.dumps(v, indent=1))

# absorber load uplift for volume cases
for cand in ['PLANT08', 'PLANT09']:
    sc = out[cand]
    print(f"\n{cand} absorber uplift (order-volume basis):")
    for q, share in sc['alloc'].items():
        moved_orders = sc['orders'] * share
        base = pg.orders.get(q, 0)
        print(f"  {q}: +{moved_orders:.0f} orders on base {base} -> uplift {100*moved_orders/base if base else float('inf'):.1f}%")

# sensitivity: PLANT16 PORT09 -> PORT04 migration re-rating
def price(lane_carrier_rows, w, n=1):
    sub = lane_carrier_rows[(lane_carrier_rows.Min_Weight_Quant <= w) & (lane_carrier_rows.Max_Weight_Quant >= w)]
    if not len(sub):
        return None
    r = sub.sort_values('Rate').iloc[0]
    return r.Min_Cost + r.Rate * w

p16 = orders[orders.Plant_Code == 'PLANT16']
cur_rows = fr[(fr.Orig_Port == 'PORT09') & (fr.Dest_Port == 'PORT09')]
new_rows = fr[(fr.Orig_Port == 'PORT04') & (fr.Dest_Port == 'PORT09')]
cur_cost = new_cost = 0.0
miss = 0
for _, o in p16.iterrows():
    w = o.Weight
    a = price(cur_rows, w)
    b = price(new_rows, w)
    if a is None:
        miss += 1
        continue
    cur_cost += a
    if b is not None:
        new_cost += b
print(f"\nPLANT16 sensitivity: priced orders={len(p16)-miss}/{len(p16)}, cur_freight=${cur_cost:,.2f}, PORT04-migration=${new_cost:,.2f}, delta=${new_cost-cur_cost:,.2f}")
print("PLANT16 wh delta if moved to PORT04 blend:", round(pg.units.get('PLANT16', 0) * (0.5383 - costd['PLANT16']), 2))

# rate card: V444_0/V444_1 coverage on PORT04->PORT09 slabs
sub = fr[(fr.Orig_Port == 'PORT04') & (fr.Dest_Port == 'PORT09')]
print("\nPORT04->PORT09 by carrier/slab:")
print(sub.groupby(['Carrier', 'Service_Level']).agg(minrate=('Rate', 'min'), maxrate=('Rate', 'max'), slabs=('Min_Weight_Quant', 'count')).round(4).to_string())

# customer concentration per candidate
for cand in CAND:
    sub = orders[orders.Plant_Code == cand]
    if len(sub):
        cc = sub.groupby('Customer').agg(n=('Order_ID', 'count'), u=('Unit_Quant', 'sum')).sort_values('n', ascending=False)
        print(f"\n{cand} customers: {cc.to_dict()}")
    else:
        print(f"\n{cand}: no orders")

# complaint/survey cross-ref for candidates
for cand in CAND:
    print(f"\n{cand} complaints:")
    print(com[com.Plant_Code == cand][['Complaint_ID', 'Customer_ID', 'Category', 'Severity', 'Resolution_Status']].to_string(index=False) if (com.Plant_Code == cand).any() else '  none')
    print(f"{cand} detractor surveys:")
    s = sur[(sur.Plant_Serviced == cand) & (sur.Would_Recommend == 'No')]
    print(s[['Response_ID', 'Customer_ID', 'Overall_Satisfaction', 'Open_Comments']].to_string(index=False) if len(s) else '  none')

[{"content": "[0] NOVATRANS LOGISTICS
[1] Delivering Excellence Across Every Mile
[3] INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
[5] DATE:  January 15, 2024
[6] TO:  Operations Consulting Team
[7] FROM:  David Chen, Chief Operating Officer, NovaTrans Logistics
[8] SUBJECT:  Engagement Brief: Distribution Network Efficiency Review
[10] 1. Background & Context
[11] NovaTrans Logistics is a mid-sized, port-based logistics company specializing in freight distribution and supply chain fulfillment. We currently operate 19 distribution plants strategically positioned across our network, handling the movement of goods between manufacturing origins, inland warehouses, and port terminals.
[12] On an annual basis, our network processes roughly 9,000+ individual shipments spanning multiple transportation modes, including SEA, AIR, and ROAD. We serve a diverse portfolio of customers under three distinct service levels:
[13] CRF (Cross-dock Freight) -- Goods are consolidated at a cross-dock facility and forwarded without long-term storage, optimizing transit speed.
[14] DTD (Door-to-Door) -- Full end-to-end delivery from origin to the customer's designated receiving location.
[15] DTP (Door-to-Port) -- Delivery from the origin point to the designated port terminal, where the customer or a third-party forwarder assumes custody.
[16] Our ERP system captures detailed transactional data for every order, including origin/destination plant codes, shipment dates, carrier assignments, freight costs, and warehouse throughput metrics. This data forms the foundation for the analysis we are requesting.
[17] 2. Problem Statement
[18] Despite steady revenue growth over the past three fiscal years, our operating margins have come under increasing pressure. Preliminary internal reviews point to several areas of concern that require rigorous, data-driven investigation:
[19] Rising Freight Costs. Overall freight expenditure has increased disproportionately relative to shipment volume. The AIR transportation mode, in particular, exhibits significantly higher per-unit costs compared to SEA and ROAD, yet continues to be utilized for shipments where alternative modes may be viable. We need a clear understanding of cost drivers across carriers and routes.
[20] Late Shipments & Customer Dissatisfaction. Approximately 2% of all orders ship late relative to their scheduled ship date. While this figure may appear modest, it translates to a meaningful number of affected customers each quarter, eroding satisfaction and jeopardizing key accounts. Our Q4 2023 customer satisfaction survey data reinforces this concern.
[21] Uneven Warehouse Utilization. Warehouse throughput varies dramatically across our plant network. For example, PLANT01 handles approximately 1,070 units per day, making it one of our highest-volume facilities, while PLANT15 processes only around 11 units per day. This imbalance raises questions about capacity allocation, fixed cost absorption, and whether certain low-volume plants should be consolidated or repurposed.
[22] Carrier & Route Cost Variability. We suspect that significant cost-efficiency differences exist between carrier-route combinations. Some carriers may deliver comparable service levels at materially lower rates on specific lanes, but we lack a consolidated view to validate this hypothesis and act on it.
[23] 3. Scope of Engagement
[24] We are engaging your team to conduct a comprehensive review of our distribution network operations. Specifically, we request that you:
[25] Analyze the order and shipment data to identify operational bottlenecks, including transit-time outliers, mode-selection inefficiencies, and demand concentration patterns.
[26] Evaluate freight cost efficiency across carriers, transportation modes, and specific origin-destination routes. Identify lanes where cost savings are achievable without degrading service quality.
[27] Assess warehouse capacity utilization across all 19 plants. Determine which facilities are over- or under-utilized relative to their stated capacity and recommend rebalancing strategies.
[28] Identify root causes of late shipments. Correlate late-shipment data with plant origin, carrier assignment, service level, and transportation mode to isolate the primary drivers of delays.
[29] Provide actionable recommendations supported by data. Each recommendation should include an estimated impact (cost savings, service improvement, or capacity optimization) and an implementation priority ranking.
[30] 4. Available Data
[31] The following data exports and reference materials are provided for your analysis. Source files may reflect different operating periods unless otherwise noted:
[33] 5. Expected Deliverables
[34] Upon completion of the engagement, we expect the following deliverables:
[35] Excel-Based Analysis Workbook. A comprehensive workbook containing separate tabs for each analytical dimension (freight cost analysis, warehouse utilization, late shipment analysis, carrier/route comparison, etc.). Composite scoring model dimensions (operationalizing "structurally unviable"):
- Volume scale (orders/units handled — low volume = weak fixed-cost absorption)
- Warehouse utilization (throughput vs capacity)
- Cost per unit (WhCosts)
- Service quality (late rate, complaints, satisfaction)
- Network redundancy (does the plant share its port(s) with other plants? If its port is unique, closing it may strand volume; if shared, volume can be absorbed)
- Cost efficiency of freight from its port

Let me define structurally unviable: a plant that combines (a) minimal scale relative to fixed cost absorption, (b) high unit handling cost or under-utilized capacity, (c) weak service performance, and (d) volume that can be feasibly absorbed by network peers (port overlap / capacity headroom).

[10] 1. Background & Context
[11] NovaTrans Logistics is a mid-sized, port-based logistics company specializing in freight distribution and supply chain fulfillment. We currently operate 19 distribution plants strategically positioned across our network, handling the movement of goods between manufacturing origins, inland warehouses, and port terminals.
[12] On an annual basis, our network processes roughly 9,000+ individual shipments spanning multiple transportation modes, including SEA, AIR, and ROAD. We serve a diverse portfolio of customers under three distinct service levels:
[13] CRF (Cross-dock Freight) -- Goods are consolidated at a cross-dock facility and forwarded without long-term storage, optimizing transit speed.
[14] DTD (Door-to-Door) -- Full end-to-end delivery from origin to the customer's designated receiving location.
[15] DTP (Door-to-Port) -- Delivery from the origin point to the designated port terminal, where the customer or a third-party forwarder assumes custody.
[16] Our ERP system captures detailed transactional data for every order, including origin/destination plant codes, shipment dates, carrier assignments, freight costs, and warehouse throughput metrics. This data forms the foundation for the analysis we are requesting.
[17] 2. Problem Statement
[18] Despite steady revenue growth over the past three fiscal years, our operating margins have come under increasing pressure. Preliminary internal reviews point to several areas of concern that require rigorous, data-driven investigation:
[19] Rising Freight Costs. Overall freight expenditure has increased disproportionately relative to shipment volume. The AIR transportation mode, in particular, exhibits significantly higher per-unit costs compared to SEA and ROAD, yet continues to be utilized for shipments where alternative modes may be viable. We need a clear understanding of cost drivers across carriers and routes.
[20] Late Shipments & Customer Dissatisfaction. Approximately 2% of all orders ship late relative to their scheduled ship date. While this figure may appear modest, it translates to a meaningful number of affected customers each quarter, eroding satisfaction and jeopardizing key accounts. Our Q4 2023 customer satisfaction survey data reinforces this concern.
[21] Uneven Warehouse Utilization. Warehouse throughput varies dramatically across our plant network. For example, PLANT01 handles approximately 1,070 units per day, making it one of our highest-volume facilities, while PLANT15 processes only around 11 units per day. This imbalance raises questions about capacity allocation, fixed cost absorption, and whether certain low-volume plants should be consolidated or repurposed.
[22] Carrier & Route Cost Variability. We suspect that significant cost-efficiency differences exist between carrier-route combinations. Some carriers may deliver comparable service levels at materially lower rates on specific lanes, but we lack a consolidated view to validate this hypothesis and act on it.
[23] 3. Scope of Engagement
[24] We are engaging your team to conduct a comprehensive review of our distribution network operations. Specifically, we request that you:
[25] Analyze the order and shipment data to identify operational bottlenecks, including transit-time outliers, mode-selection inefficiencies, and demand concentration patterns.
[26] Evaluate freight cost efficiency across carriers, transportation modes, and specific origin-destination routes. Identify lanes where cost savings are achievable without degrading service quality.
[27] Assess warehouse capacity utilization across all 19 plants. Determine which facilities are over- or under-utilized relative to their stated capacity and recommend rebalancing strategies.
[28] Identify root causes of late shipments. Correlate late-shipment data with plant origin, carrier assignment, service level, and transportation mode to isolate the primary drivers of delays.
[29] Provide actionable recommendations supported by data. Each recommendation should include an estimated impact (cost savings, service improvement, or capacity optimization) and an implementation priority ranking.

[{"content": "[0] NOVATRANS LOGISTICS
[1] Delivering Excellence Across Every Mile
[3] INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
[5] DATE:  January 15, 2024
[6] TO:  Operations Consulting Team
[7] FROM:  David Chen, Chief Operating Officer, NovaTrans Logistics
[8] SUBJECT:  Engagement Brief: Distribution Network Efficiency Review
[10] 1. Background & Context
[11] NovaTrans Logistics is a mid-sized, port-based logistics company specializing in freight distribution and supply chain fulfillment. We currently operate 19 distribution plants strategically positioned across our network, handling the movement of goods between manufacturing origins, inland warehouses, and port terminals.
[12] On an annual basis, our network processes roughly 9,000+ individual shipments spanning multiple transportation modes, including SEA, AIR, and ROAD. We serve a diverse portfolio of customers under three distinct service levels:
[13] CRF (Cross-dock Freight) -- Goods are consolidated at a cross-dock facility and forwarded without long-term storage, optimizing transit speed.
[14] DTD (Door-to-Door) -- Full end-to-end delivery from origin to the customer's designated receiving location.
[15] DTP (Door-to-Port) -- Delivery from the origin point to the designated port terminal, where the customer or a third-party forwarder assumes custody.
[16] Our ERP system captures detailed transactional data for every order, including origin/destination plant codes, shipment dates, carrier assignments, freight costs, and warehouse throughput metrics. This data forms the foundation for the analysis we are requesting.
[17] 2. Problem Statement
[18] Despite steady revenue growth over the past three fiscal years, our operating margins have come under increasing pressure. Preliminary internal reviews point to several areas of concern that require rigorous, data-driven investigation:
[19] Rising Freight Costs. Overall freight expenditure has increased disproportionately relative to shipment volume. The AIR transportation mode, in particular, exhibits significantly higher per-unit costs compared to SEA and ROAD, yet continues to be utilized for shipments where alternative modes may be viable. We need a clear understanding of cost drivers across carriers and routes.
[20] Late Shipments & Customer Dissatisfaction. Approximately 2% of all orders ship late relative to their scheduled ship date. While this figure may appear modest, it translates to a meaningful number of affected customers each quarter, eroding satisfaction and jeopardizing key accounts. Our Q4 2023 customer satisfaction survey data reinforces this concern.
[21] Uneven Warehouse Utilization. Warehouse throughput varies dramatically across our plant network. For example, PLANT01 handles approximately 1,070 units per day, making it one of our highest-volume facilities, while PLANT15 processes only around 11 units per day. This imbalance raises questions about capacity allocation, fixed cost absorption, and whether certain low-volume plants should be consolidated or repurposed.
[22] Carrier & Route Cost Variability. We suspect that significant cost-efficiency differences exist between carrier-route combinations. Some carriers may deliver comparable service levels at materially lower rates on specific lanes, but we lack a consolidated view to validate this hypothesis and act on it.
[23] 3. Scope of Engagement
[24] We are engaging your team to conduct a comprehensive review of our distribution network operations. Specifically, we request that you:
[25] Analyze the order and shipment data to identify operational bottlenecks, including transit-time outliers, mode-selection inefficiencies, and demand concentration patterns.
[26] Evaluate freight cost efficiency across carriers, transportation modes, and specific origin-destination routes. Identify lanes where cost savings are achievable without degrading service quality.
[27] Assess warehouse capacity utilization across all 19 plants. Determine which facilities are over- or under-utilized relative to their stated capacity and recommend rebalancing strategies.
[28] Identify root causes of late shipments. Correlate late-shipment data with plant origin, carrier assignment, service level, and transportation mode to isolate the primary drivers of delays.
[29] Provide actionable recommendations supported by data. Each recommendation should include an estimated impact (cost savings, service improvement, or capacity optimization) and an implementation priority ranking.
[30] 4. Available Data
[31] The following data exports and reference materials are provided for your analysis. Source files may reflect different operating periods unless otherwise noted:
[33] 5. Expected Deliverables
[34] Upon completion of the engagement, we expect the following deliverables:
[35] Excel-Based Analysis Workbook. A comprehensive workbook containing separate tabs for each analytical dimension (freight cost analysis, warehouse utilization, late shipment analysis, carrier/route comparison, etc.). Each tab should include source data summaries, pivot analyses, charts where appropriate, and key findings highlighted in a consistent format.
[36] Executive Summary Report (Word Document). A standalone Word document (maximum 10 pages) summarizing the engagement findings, key insights, and prioritized recommendations. This document will be circulated to the executive leadership team and should be written at a level appropriate for a C-suite audience. Include an executive summary on the first page, followed by detailed sections for each analytical area, and conclude with a prioritized action plan.
[37] 6. Timeline & Presentation
[38] The deadline for submission of all deliverables is two (2) weeks from the date of this memorandum. Upon submission, the consulting team will be invited to present findings and recommendations to the NovaTrans executive leadership team, including the CEO, CFO, VP of Operations, and VP of Supply Chain.
[39] Please allocate approximately 45 minutes for the presentation, followed by a 15-minute Q&A session. Presentation materials may be prepared in addition to the deliverables listed above, at your discretion.
[40] 7. Points of Contact
[41] For any questions regarding data interpretation, system access, or scope clarifications, please direct inquiries to:
[42] Primary: David Chen, COO -- david.chen@novatrans-logistics.com
[43] Secondary: Maria Santos, Director of Operations -- maria.santos@novatrans-logistics.com
[44] Data/IT: James Park, Senior Data Analyst -- james.park@novatrans-logistics.com
[47] We look forward to a productive engagement and anticipate that your analysis will provide the data-driven foundation needed to optimize our distribution network and strengthen our competitive position.
[49] Regards,
[51] David Chen
[52] Chief Operating Officer
[53] NovaTrans Logistics

{"content": "import pandas as pd, numpy as np

orders = pd.read_csv('/work/task_folder/OrderList.csv')
cap = pd.read_csv('/work/task_folder/references/WhCapacities.csv')
cost = pd.read_csv('/work/task_folder/references/WhCosts.csv')
pp = pd.read_csv('/work/task_folder/PlantPorts.csv')
fr = pd.read_csv('/work/task_folder/references/FreightRates.csv')
fr.columns = [c.strip() for c in fr.columns]
fr['Mode_DSC'] = fr['Mode_DSC'].str.strip()
sur = pd.read_excel('/work/task_folder/Customer_Satisfaction_Survey_Q4.xlsx', sheet_name='Survey_Results')
com = pd.read_excel('/work/task_folder/Customer_Satisfaction_Survey_Q4.xlsx', sheet_name='Complaint_Log')

plants = sorted(cap.Plant_Code.unique())
ports = pp.groupby('Plant_Code')['Ports'].apply(list).to_dict()
port_plants = pp.groupby('Ports')['Plant_Code'].apply(list).to_dict()
capd = dict(zip(cap.Plant_Code, cap.Daily_Capacity))
costd = dict(zip(cost.Plant_Code, cost.Cost_Per_Unit))

g = orders.groupby('Plant_Code').agg(orders=('Order_ID', 'count'), units=('Unit_Quant', 'sum'),
    weight=('Weight', 'sum'), customers=('Customer', 'nunique'),
    late=('Ship_Late_Day_Count', lambda s: (s > 0).sum()))
g['late_rate'] = g.late / g.orders
units_total = orders.Unit_Quant.sum()

N = len(plants)
logcap = np.log(np.array([capd[p] for p in plants], dtype=float))
s_scale = 100 * (1 - (logcap - logcap.min()) / (logcap.max() - logcap.min()))
c = np.array([costd[p] for p in plants])
s_cost = 100 * (c - c.min()) / (c.max() - c.min())
s_abs = []
for p in plants:
    peer_set = set()
    for pt in ports[p]:
        peer_set |= set(port_plants[pt])
    peer_set.discard(p)
    peer_cap = sum(capd[q] for q in peer_set)
    own = capd[p]
    s_abs.append(100 * peer_cap / (peer_cap + own) if peer_cap + own > 0 else 0)
s_abs = np.array(s_abs)
s_dem = np.array([100 * (1 - g.units.get(p, 0) / units_total) for p in plants])

sev_map = {'High': 3, 'Medium': 2, 'Low': 1}
com['sev_w'] = com.Severity.map(sev_map)
comp_by_plant = com.groupby('Plant_Code').agg(n=('Complaint_ID', 'count'), w=('sev_w', 'sum'),
    open_n=('Resolution_Status', lambda s: (s != 'Resolved').sum()))
sur['det'] = (sur.Would_Recommend == 'No').astype(int)
sur_by_plant = sur.groupby('Plant_Serviced').agg(resp=('Response_ID', 'count'), det=('det', 'sum'), sat=('Overall_Satisfaction', 'mean'))
max_late = g.late_rate.max() if g.late_rate.max() > 0 else 1
s_srv = []
for p in plants:
    if p in g.index:
        late_sc = 100 * g.late_rate.get(p, 0) / max_late
        cw_sc = 100 * comp_by_plant.w.get(p, 0) / com.sev_w.sum()
        det_sc = 100 * sur_by_plant.det.get(p, 0) / sur_by_plant.resp.get(p, 1) if p in sur_by_plant.index else 0
        s_srv.append(0.4 * late_sc + 0.3 * cw_sc + 0.3 * det_sc)
    else:
        s_srv.append(50.0)
s_srv = np.array(s_srv)

W = {'scale': 0.25, 'cost': 0.20, 'absorb': 0.20, 'demand': 0.15, 'service': 0.20}
comp = W['scale'] * s_scale + W['cost'] * s_cost + W['absorb'] * s_abs + W['demand'] * s_dem + W['service'] * s_srv
res = pd.DataFrame({'Plant': plants, 'Daily_Capacity': [capd[p] for p in plants],
    'Cost_per_Unit': [round(costd[p], 4) for p in plants],
    'Ports': [';'.join(ports[p]) for p in plants],
    'SamePort_Plants': [len(set([q for pt in ports[p] for q in port_plants[pt]]) - {p}) for p in plants],
    'Obs_Orders': [g.orders.get(p, 0) for p in plants],
    'Obs_Units': [g.units.get(p, 0) for p in plants],
    'S_scale': s_scale.round(1), 'S_cost': s_cost.round(1), 'S_absorb': s_abs.round(1),
    'S_demand': s_dem.round(1), 'S_service': s_srv.round(1), 'Composite': comp.round(1)
    }).sort_values('Composite', ascending=False)
res['Rank'] = range(1, N + 1)
print(res.to_string(index=False))
res.to_csv('/work/work/composite.csv', index=False)
print("\nComplaints by plant:\n", comp_by_plant.to_string())
print("\nSurvey by plant:\n", sur_by_plant.round(2).to_string())
print("\nTotal stated capacity:", cap.Daily_Capacity.sum())
print("Units total:", units_total, "Orders:", len(orders))

[{"content": "[0] NOVATRANS LOGISTICS
[1] Delivering Excellence Across Every Mile
[3] INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
[5] DATE:  January 15, 2024
[6] TO:  Operations Consulting Team
[7] FROM:  David Chen, Chief Operating Officer, NovaTrans Logistics
[8] SUBJECT:  Engagement Brief: Distribution Network Efficiency Review
[10] 1. Background & Context
[11] NovaTrans Logistics is a mid-sized, port-based logistics company specializing in freight distribution and supply chain fulfillment. We currently operate 19 distribution plants strategically positioned across our network, handling the movement of goods between manufacturing origins, inland warehouses, and port terminals.
[12] On an annual basis, our network processes roughly 9,000+ individual shipments spanning multiple transportation modes, including SEA, AIR, and ROAD. We serve a diverse portfolio of customers under three distinct service levels:
[13] CRF (Cross-dock Freight) -- Goods are consolidated at a cross-dock facility and forwarded without long-term storage, optimizing transit speed.
[14] DTD (Door-to-Door) -- Full end-to-end delivery from origin to the customer's designated receiving location.
[15] DTP (Door-to-Port) -- Delivery from the origin point to the designated port terminal, where the customer or a third-party forwarder assumes custody.
[16] Our ERP system captures detailed transactional data for every order, including origin/destination plant codes, shipment dates, carrier assignments, freight costs, and warehouse throughput metrics. This data forms the foundation for the analysis we are requesting.
[17] 2. Problem Statement
[18] Despite steady revenue growth over the past three fiscal years, our operating margins have come under increasing pressure. Preliminary internal reviews point to several areas of concern that require rigorous, data-driven investigation:
[19] Rising Freight Costs. Overall freight expenditure has increased disproportionately relative to shipment volume. The AIR transportation mode, in particular, exhibits significantly higher per-unit costs compared to SEA and ROAD, yet continues to be utilized for shipments where alternative modes may be viable. We need a clear understanding of cost drivers across carriers and routes.
[20] Late Shipments & Customer Dissatisfaction. Approximately 2% of all orders ship late relative to their scheduled ship date. While this figure may appear modest, it translates to a meaningful number of affected customers each quarter, eroding satisfaction and jeopardizing key accounts. Our Q4 2023 customer satisfaction survey data reinforces this concern.
[21] Uneven Warehouse Utilization. Warehouse throughput varies dramatically across our plant network. For example, PLANT01 handles approximately 1,070 units per day, making it one of our highest-volume facilities, while PLANT15 processes only around 11 units per day. This imbalance raises questions about capacity allocation, fixed cost absorption, and whether certain low-volume plants should be consolidated or repurposed.
[22] Carrier & Route Cost Variability. We suspect that significant cost-efficiency differences exist between carrier-route combinations. Some carriers may deliver comparable service levels at materially lower rates on specific lanes, but we lack a consolidated view to validate this hypothesis and act on it.
[23] 3. Scope of Engagement
[24] We are engaging your team to conduct a comprehensive review of our distribution network operations. Specifically, we request that you:
[25] Analyze the order and shipment data to identify operational bottlenecks, including transit-time outliers, mode-selection inefficiencies, and demand concentration patterns.
[26] Evaluate freight cost efficiency across carriers, transportation modes, and specific origin-destination routes. Identify lanes where cost savings are achievable without degrading service quality.
[27] Assess warehouse capacity utilization across all 19 plants. Determine which facilities are over- or under-utilized relative to their stated capacity and recommend rebalancing strategies.
[28] Identify root causes of late shipments. Correlate late-shipment data with plant origin, carrier assignment, service level, and transportation mode to isolate the primary drivers of delays.
[29] Provide actionable recommendations supported by data. Each recommendation should include an estimated impact (cost savings, service improvement, or capacity optimization) and an implementation priority ranking.
[30] 4. Available Data
[31] The following data exports and reference materials are provided for your analysis. Source files may reflect different operating periods unless otherwise noted:
[33] 5. Expected Deliverables
[34] Upon completion of the engagement, we expect the following deliverables:
[35] Excel-Based Analysis Workbook. A comprehensive workbook containing separate tabs for each analytical dimension (freight cost analysis, warehouse utilization, late shipment analysis, carrier/route comparison, etc.). Each tab should include source data summaries, pivot analyses, charts where appropriate, and key findings highlighted in a consistent format.
[36] Executive Summary Report (Word Document). A standalone Word document (maximum 10 pages) summarizing the engagement findings, key insights, and prioritized recommendations. This document will be circulated to the executive leadership team and should be written at a level appropriate for a C-suite audience. Include an executive summary on the first page, followed by detailed sections for each analytical area, and conclude with a prioritized action plan.
[37] 6. Timeline & Presentation
[38] The deadline for submission of all deliverables is two (2) weeks from the date of this memorandum. Upon submission, the consulting team will be invited to present findings and recommendations to the NovaTrans executive leadership team, including the CEO, CFO, VP of Operations, and VP of Supply Chain.
[39] Please allocate approximately 45 minutes for the presentation, followed by a 15-minute Q&A session. Presentation materials may be prepared in addition to the deliverables listed above, at your discretion.
[40] 7. Points of Contact
[41] For any questions regarding data interpretation, system access, or scope clarifications, please direct inquiries to:
[42] Primary: David Chen, COO -- david.chen@novatrans-logistics.com
[43] Secondary: Maria Santos, Director of Operations -- maria.santos@novatrans-logistics.com
[44] Data/IT: James Park, Senior Data Analyst -- james.park@novatrans-logistics.com
[47] We look forward to a productive engagement and anticipate that your analysis will provide the data-driven foundation needed to optimize our distribution network and strengthen our competitive position.
[49] Regards,
[51] David Chen
[52] Chief Operating Officer
[53] NovaTrans Logistics

[8] SUBJECT:  Engagement Brief: Distribution Network Efficiency Review
[10] 1. Background & Context
[11] NovaTrans Logistics is a mid-sized, port-based logistics company specializing in freight distribution and supply chain fulfillment. We currently operate 19 distribution plants strategically positioned across our network, handling the movement of goods between manufacturing origins, inland warehouses, and port terminals.
[12] On an annual basis, our network processes roughly 9,000+ individual shipments spanning multiple transportation modes, including SEA, AIR, and ROAD. We serve a diverse portfolio of customers under three distinct service levels:
[13] CRF (Cross-dock Freight) -- Goods are consolidated at a cross-dock facility and forwarded without long-term storage, optimizing transit speed.
[14] DTD (Door-to-Door) -- Full end-to-end delivery from origin to the customer's designated receiving location.
[15] DTP (Door-to-Port) -- Delivery from the origin point to the designated port terminal, where the customer or a third-party forwarder assumes custody.
[16] Our ERP system captures detailed transactional data for every order, including origin/destination plant codes, shipment dates, carrier assignments, freight costs, and warehouse throughput metrics. This data forms the foundation for the analysis we are requesting.
[17] 2. Problem Statement
[18] Despite steady revenue growth over the past three fiscal years, our operating margins have come under increasing pressure. Preliminary internal reviews point to several areas of concern that require rigorous, data-driven investigation:
[19] Rising Freight Costs. Overall freight expenditure has increased disproportionately relative to shipment volume. The AIR transportation mode, in particular, exhibits significantly higher per-unit costs compared to SEA and ROAD, yet continues to be utilized for shipments where alternative modes may be viable. We need a clear understanding of cost drivers across carriers and routes.
[20] Late Shipments & Customer Dissatisfaction. Approximately 2% of all orders ship late relative to their scheduled ship date. While this figure may appear modest, it translates to a meaningful number of affected customers each quarter, eroding satisfaction and jeopardizing key accounts. Our Q4 2023 customer satisfaction survey data reinforces this concern.
[21] Uneven Warehouse Utilization. Warehouse throughput varies dramatically across our plant network. For example, PLANT01 handles approximately 1,070 units per day, making it one of our highest-volume facilities, while PLANT15 processes only around 11 units per day. This imbalance raises questions about capacity allocation, fixed cost absorption, and whether certain low-volume plants should be consolidated or repurposed.
[22] Carrier & Route Cost Variability. We suspect that significant cost-efficiency differences exist between carrier-route combinations. Some carriers may deliver comparable service levels at materially lower rates on specific lanes, but we lack a consolidated view to validate this hypothesis and act on it.
[23] 3. Scope of Engagement
[24] We are engaging your team to conduct a comprehensive review of our distribution network operations. Specifically, we request that you:
[25] Analyze the order and shipment data to identify operational bottlenecks, including transit-time outliers, mode-selection inefficiencies, and demand concentration patterns.
[26] Evaluate freight cost efficiency across carriers, transportation modes, and specific origin-destination routes. Identify lanes where cost savings are achievable without degrading service quality.
[27] Assess warehouse capacity utilization across all 19 plants. Determine which facilities are over- or under-utilized relative to their stated capacity and recommend rebalancing strategies.
[28] Identify root causes of late shipments. Correlate late-shipment data with plant origin, carrier assignment, service level, and transportation mode to isolate the primary drivers of delays.
[29] Provide actionable recommendations supported by data. Each recommendation should include an estimated impact (cost savings, service improvement, or capacity optimization) and an implementation priority ranking.
[30] 4. Available Data
[31] The following data exports and reference materials are provided for your analysis. Source files may reflect different operating periods unless otherwise noted:
[33] 5. Expected Deliverables
[34] Upon completion of the engagement, we expect the following deliverables:
[35] Excel-Based Analysis Workbook. A comprehensive workbook containing separate tabs for each analytical dimension (freight cost analysis, warehouse utilization, late shipment analysis, carrier/route comparison, etc.). Each tab should include source data summaries, pivot analyses, charts where appropriate, and key findings highlighted in a consistent format.
[36] Executive Summary Report (Word Document). A standalone Word document (maximum 10 pages) summarizing the engagement findings, key insights, and prioritized recommendations. This document will be circulated to the executive leadership team and should be written at a level appropriate for a C-suite audience. Include an executive summary on the first page, followed by detailed sections for each analytical area, and conclude with a prioritized action plan.
[37] 6. Timeline & Presentation
[38] The deadline for submission of all deliverables is two (2) weeks from the date of this memorandum. Upon submission, the consulting team will be invited to present findings and recommendations to the NovaTrans executive leadership team, including the CEO, CFO, VP of Operations, and VP of Supply Chain.
[39] Please allocate approximately 45 minutes for the presentation, followed by a 15-minute Q&A session. Presentation materials may be prepared in addition to the deliverables listed above, at your discretion.

Wait — this is the classic "supply chain logistics problem" dataset from Brunel. The OrderList only includes plants connected to PORT09 (dest). [13] CRF (Cross-dock Freight) -- Goods are consolidated at a cross-dock facility and forwarded without long-term storage, optimizing transit speed.
[14] DTD (Door-to-Door) -- Full end-to-end delivery from origin to the customer's designated receiving location.
[15] DTP (Door-to-Port) -- Delivery from the origin point to the designated port terminal, where the customer or a third-party forwarder assumes custody.
[16] Our ERP system captures detailed transactional data for every order, including origin/destination plant codes, shipment dates, carrier assignments, freight costs, and warehouse throughput metrics. This data forms the foundation for the analysis we are requesting.
[17] 2. Problem Statement
[18] Despite steady revenue growth over the past three fiscal years, our operating margins have come under increasing pressure. Preliminary internal reviews point to several areas of concern that require rigorous, data-driven investigation:
[19] Rising Freight Costs. Overall freight expenditure has increased disproportionately relative to shipment volume. We need a clear understanding of cost drivers across carriers and routes.
[20] Late Shipments & Customer Dissatisfaction. Approximately 2% of all orders ship late relative to their scheduled ship date. While this figure may appear modest, it translates to a meaningful number of affected customers each quarter, eroding satisfaction and jeopardizing key accounts. [21] Uneven Warehouse Utilization. Warehouse throughput varies dramatically across our plant network. [28] Identify root causes of late shipments. Correlate late-shipment data with plant origin, carrier assignment, service level, and transportation mode to isolate the primary drivers of delays.
